title: Nationwide prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus and cervical cytology findings in Chile: a registry-based study (2019–2024)
abstract: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV), remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death in women globally. No nationwide analysis has integrated molecular HPV testing and cervical cytology using registry-based data. The aim of the present study was to provide the first nationwide registry-based estimate of HR-HPV positivity and age-specific cervical cytological abnormalities within the Chilean National Cervical Cancer Screening Program. A retrospective descriptive analysis was conducted using nationwide aggregate data from the Chilean Ministry of Health (MINSAL), covering the nationwide cervical cancer screening network. A total of 506 712 cervical samples tested for HR-HPV (2020–2024) and 4 055 738 adequate Papanicolaou (PAP) tests (2019–2024) were analyzed. The HR-HPV positivity between 2020 and 2024 was 13.02% (95% confidence interval: 12.93–13.11%), with annual values of 12.34, 12.73, 13.27, 13.47, and 12.85% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. The highest HPV prevalence was observed in G1 (30–44 years), ranging from 15.39 to 16.26%, compared with 8.95–10.55% in G2 (45–64 years) and 5.46–13.30% in G3 (≥65 years). Among all HPV-positive women, HPV-16 accounted for 19.57% of infections, HPV-18 for 6.39%, and pooled HR-HPV types for 74.03%. Regarding PAP results, 95.63% of adequate tests were classified as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, while low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) (NIE I) was found in 0.77%, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (NIE II) in 0.33%, and severe HSIL (NIE III) in 0.26% of cases. This nationwide registry-based study establishes the first comprehensive baseline of HR-HPV positivity and cervical cytology in Chile. The predominance of non-16/18 h-HPV infections reinforces the importance of broad-spectrum extended HPV genotyping surveillance and provides a benchmark for evaluating the long-term impact of HPV vaccination and implementation of primary HPV screening.

title: Building Demand for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination in India: A Review of the Behavioural and Social Drivers of Parental and Community Acceptance
abstract: India launched its National HPV Vaccination Campaign in February 2026, offering free, voluntary, singledose vaccination to 14-year-old girls with parental consent.By September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered against an estimated annual cohort of about 1.2 crore girls, with wide variation across states.Because uptake depends on parental decisions, understanding what drives acceptance is now a programme priority rather than an academic question.This narrative review synthesises Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search and organised by the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework, and considers how the shift to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme changes the relevance of earlier findings.Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity.Decisions are shaped by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers.Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts.Before 2026, cost was a dominant practical barrier; with free provision, the remaining practical barriers are mostly access, consent processes, and reaching girls outside school.The national campaign removes the cost barrier but not the belief-based and social barriers.Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy.Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on understanding the behavioural and social drivers of parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in India, particularly in the context of the newly launched National HPV Vaccination Campaign. The central question is how these drivers influence vaccination uptake among 14-year-old girls, with an emphasis on the shift from a cost-based to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of HPV vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search. The evidence is organised using the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but synthesises findings from a limited number of studies, primarily concentrated in southern districts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity. Decisions are influenced by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers. The national campaign removes the cost barrier but does not address belief-based and social barriers, which remain significant.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts, limiting generalisability. There is wide variation in uptake across states, and the review notes that the shift to a free programme changes the relevance of earlier findings. The evidence does not address the role of specific HPV types or their association with diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy. Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the behavioural and social factors influencing parental and community acceptance of HPV vaccination in India, focusing on the National HPV Vaccination Campaign launched in 2026. It highlights low awareness, safety concerns, and fears about infertility as key barriers, with family influence and health worker recommendations playing significant roles. While the campaign removes cost barriers, belief-based and social barriers persist. The review underscores the need for targeted strategies to improve demand, including engaging community leaders, addressing misinformation, and standardising behavioural assessments. Evidence is limited to southern districts and relies on stated willingness rather than actual vaccination rates, indicating a need for more comprehensive data collection.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述的重点是了解印度家长和社区接受 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 的行为和社会驱动因素,特别是在新发起的全国 HPV 疫苗接种 运动的背景下。核心问题是这些驱动因素如何影响 14 岁女孩对 疫苗接种 的接受,重点是从基于成本的计划向免费、国家认可的单剂量计划的转变。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对印度父母和社区接受 HPV 疫苗接种 证据的叙述性综合,这些证据是通过结构化 PubMed 搜索确定的。证据是使用世界卫生组织 (WHO) 行为和社会驱动因素 (BeSD) 框架进行组织的。该综述没有报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是综合了数量有限的研究结果,这些研究主要集中在南部地区。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 印度的研究一致报告称,人们的意识较低,对安全和不孕不育的担忧,以及对 疫苗 可能鼓励早期性活动的担忧。决定受到更广泛的家庭的影响,父亲和长辈往往拥有最终决定权,并受到医生和一线工作人员建议的影响。全国运动消除了成本障碍,但没有解决基于信仰和社会的障碍,这些障碍仍然很重要。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 大多数研究衡量的是陈述的意愿而不是实际的 疫苗接种,而且证据集中在南部的几个地区,限制了普遍性。各州的接受程度存在很大差异,审查指出,向免费计划的转变改变了早期发现的相关性。证据并未涉及特定 HPV 类型的作用或其与宫颈上皮内瘤变或 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 等疾病的关联。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on understanding the behavioural and social drivers of parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in India, particularly in the context of the newly launched National HPV Vaccination Campaign. The central question is how these drivers influence vaccination uptake among 14-year-old girls, with an emphasis on the shift from a cost-based to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of HPV vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search. The evidence is organised using the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but synthesises findings from a limited number of studies, primarily concentrated in southern districts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity. Decisions are influenced by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers. The national campaign removes the cost barrier but does not address belief-based and social barriers, which remain significant.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts, limiting generalisability. There is wide variation in uptake across states, and the review notes that the shift to a free programme changes the relevance of earlier findings. The evidence does not address the role of specific HPV types or their association with diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or HPV-associated cervical cancer.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy. Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring.

media_mentions.content_title: Building Demand for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination in India: A Review of the Behavioural and Social Drivers of Parental and Community Acceptance
media_mentions.content: Abstract India launched its National HPV Vaccination Campaign in February 2026, offering free, voluntary, single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls with parental consent. By September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered against an estimated annual cohort of about 1.2 crore girls, with wide variation across states. Because uptake depends on parental decisions, understanding what drives acceptance is now a programme priority rather than an academic question. This narrative review synthesises Indian evidence on parental and community acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, identified through a structured PubMed search and organised by the World Health Organization (WHO) Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework, and considers how the shift to a free, nationally endorsed, single-dose programme changes the relevance of earlier findings. Indian studies consistently report low awareness, fears about safety and infertility, and concerns that the vaccine may encourage early sexual activity. Decisions are shaped by the wider family, with fathers and elders often having the final say, and by the recommendations of doctors and frontline workers. Most studies measure stated willingness rather than actual vaccination, and the evidence is concentrated in a few southern districts. Before 2026, cost was a dominant practical barrier; with free provision, the remaining practical barriers are mostly access, consent processes, and reaching girls outside school. The national campaign removes the cost barrier but not the belief-based and social barriers. Demand generation should prioritise equipping trusted health workers and teachers to recommend vaccination, engaging extended families and community leaders, pre-empting misinformation, and making consent and access easy. Standardised measurement of behavioural drivers, using tools such as the WHO BeSD surveys, should be built into campaign monitoring. Introduction & Background Cervical cancer is among the most common cancers in Indian women and accounts for a substantial share of the global burden [1]. It is also among the most preventable. The World Health Organization (WHO) strategy to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem sets three targets for 2030: 90% of girls fully vaccinated against human papillomavirus (HPV) by the age of 15 years, 70% of women screened with a high-performance test by the ages of 35 and 45 years, and 90% of women with cervical disease receiving treatment [2]. India has contributed decisively to the science of HPV vaccination. The multicentre cohort in India coordinated by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) showed that a single dose of quadrivalent HPV vaccine protected adolescent girls against persistent HPV 16/18 infection as well as two or three doses at 10 years, with a single-dose vaccine efficacy of 95.4% [3,4]. This evidence underpinned the global shift to single-dose schedules. India has also developed an indigenous quadrivalent vaccine that was shown to be non-inferior to an established vaccine in a phase 2/3 trial [5]. Before the national programme, HPV vaccination in India was limited. It was available mainly in the private sector and through state initiatives such as those in Punjab and Sikkim [6,7]. A meta-analysis of community-level studies estimated pooled coverage of only about 4%; in the same meta-analysis, only about 22% of respondents had knowledge of the vaccine, and 45% had a positive attitude towards it [8]. This changed in February 2026, when the National HPV Vaccination Campaign was launched. It offers free, voluntary, single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities, with parental consent. According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered by 11 September 2026, against an annual cohort of about 1.2 crore 14-year-old girls estimated from Registrar General of India projections; Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Mizoram reported covering 100% of their identified target populations, while coverage in other states was lower [9]. Because the campaign is voluntary and consent-based, its success depends on the decisions of parents and on the people who influence them. Vaccine hesitancy, defined as delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite available services, is complex and context-specific, and it varies across time, place, and vaccine [10]. Most Indian studies on HPV vaccine acceptance were conducted when the vaccine was paid for, multi-dose, and not endorsed by a national programme. It is therefore important to ask which of their findings still apply. A recent scoping review mapped barriers to HPV vaccination among adolescent girls in India, covering studies published between 2008 and 2025 and organising them by the socio-ecological model [11]. The present review differs from it in three respects. First, its focus is the decision-makers and influencers around the girl, namely, parents, extended families, teachers, and health workers, rather than the girl alone. Second, it organises the evidence using the WHO Behavioural and Social Drivers (BeSD) framework, which immunisation programmes themselves use to design and monitor demand generation, so that each finding can be linked to a programme action. Third, it interprets the evidence in light of the national single-dose campaign, asking which barriers the campaign removes and which remain, and it includes studies published in 2025 and 2026 around the time of national introduction. The aim of this narrative review is therefore to synthesise Indian evidence on the behavioural and social drivers of parental and community acceptance of HPV vaccination, to examine how the national campaign changes their relevance, and to derive practical recommendations for demand generation and research. The review is a narrative synthesis of published quantitative and qualitative studies; it does not pool data statistically. The review was prepared in line with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) [12]. PubMed was searched on 2 October 2026 for articles published from January 2008 onward, using Medical Subject Headings and free-text terms for HPV vaccine, acceptance or hesitancy, and India combined with Boolean operators; the full search string is given in Appendix 1. Studies were eligible if they were conducted in India and reported acceptance, willingness, intention, hesitancy, or uptake of HPV vaccination for adolescents, or the determinants of these, among parents or caregivers, adolescents, or community influencers such as teachers and health workers; intervention studies and programme evaluations with an acceptance outcome were also eligible. Studies conducted outside India, studies of adults, students, or health workers considering vaccination for themselves, studies reporting knowledge alone, and studies of cervical screening or economic modelling were excluded. Titles and abstracts were screened by one author, and decisions and reasons for exclusion were recorded in a screening log. Of 176 records retrieved, 119 were excluded, 16 were retained as background sources, and 41 were judged relevant, comprising 38 primary studies and three prior syntheses (Appendix 2). The search was supplemented by the reference lists of recent Indian reviews [8,11], policy documents from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and WHO, and targeted searches for international evidence on vaccine confidence and misinformation. Studies were selected for discussion according to their relevance to each BeSD domain, giving preference to larger samples, analytical designs, and recent studies; findings were then synthesised narratively under each domain. Review Conceptual framework: the behavioural and social drivers of vaccination The BeSD framework, developed by WHO and built on the work of Brewer and colleagues, groups the drivers of vaccination into four domains [13,14]. The first domain, thinking and feeling, covers perceived disease risk, vaccine confidence, and trust. The second, social processes, covers social norms, recommendations from health workers, and who makes decisions within the family. The third, motivation, refers to the intention or willingness to vaccinate. The fourth, practical issues, covers availability, affordability, ease of access, and the quality of the service experience. Within this framework, thoughts, feelings, and social processes are understood to shape motivation, while practical issues determine whether motivation turns into vaccination [13,14]. Evidence synthesised by Brewer and colleagues, drawn mainly from high-income countries, suggests that interventions that build on existing favourable intentions and make vaccination easy tend to be more effective than attempts to change people's minds [14]. The framework is particularly useful in India because it aligns with the survey tools that immunisation programmes can use to monitor drivers of uptake. Table 1 summarises the key Indian primary studies discussed in this review, including their settings, designs, populations, and principal findings. Thinking and feeling: awareness, risk perception, and vaccine confidence Low Awareness and Low Perceived Risk Across Indian studies, awareness of HPV, of its link to cervical cancer, and of the vaccine has been consistently low among parents, adolescents, and women [8,11]. Low awareness reduces perceived risk. When parents do not see cervical cancer as a threat relevant to their daughters, the vaccine offers little apparent benefit. Most studies treat awareness as a prerequisite for acceptance, but educational interventions show that raising knowledge does not always translate into a decision to vaccinate. In a school-based study in Mysuru, for example, an educational leaflet sent to parents significantly improved their knowledge but did not change their perception of the vaccine [19]. Safety Concerns and Infertility Fears Concerns about side effects are among the most frequently reported reasons for hesitancy in Indian studies [11,15,18]. In a 2010 survey of 797 parents of schoolgirls in Mysore, those who had concerns about side effects were less likely to report willingness to accept the vaccine, while those who believed it was safe were more likely to accept it [15]. A specific and recurring fear is that the vaccine may affect future fertility. This concern carries particular weight in a society where marriage and childbearing are central to a girl's future. The belief appears in several settings and is often linked to wider mistrust of new vaccines given to adolescent girls [11]. The Shadow of 2010 Parental trust in HPV vaccination in India cannot be separated from its history. In April 2010, the government suspended HPV vaccine demonstration projects in Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat amid public concerns about safety [25,26]. The suspension also halted the IARC multicentre trial, which was then converted into a cohort study [3]. The episode was widely debated, including challenges to the epidemiological case for vaccination at the time [26]. It shaped professional and public discussion of the vaccine for more than a decade, and it remains a ready source for misinformation. Moral Concerns Because HPV is sexually transmitted, some parents believe that vaccinating daughters may signal permission for, or encourage, early sexual activity. Several Indian studies report this concern, and the associated stigma is strongest in conservative and rural settings [11]. This is one reason why framing HPV vaccination as cancer prevention, rather than prevention of a sexually transmitted infection, recurs in the recommendations below. Social processes: who decides and who influences Family Decision-Making HPV vaccination decisions in Indian families are rarely made by one person alone. In Mysore, parents were more likely to accept the vaccine for their daughters when their own parents recommended it, and the authors called for promotion directed at the extended family [15]. A more recent qualitative study in a district of Rajasthan, based on six focus group discussions with parents and frontline workers and 10 in-depth interviews with medical officers and teachers, found that decision-making was family-based, with mothers acting as information seekers and fathers often perceived as the final decision-makers [24]. Family disapproval, particularly in conservative settings, has been linked to refusal [11]. Communication strategies aimed only at mothers, or only at girls through schools, may therefore miss the people who actually shape the decision. The Power of a Recommendation In international evidence, a recommendation from a trusted health provider is one of the strongest predictors of vaccine acceptance [14]. Indian studies echo this. In 36 qualitative interviews, parents reported being strongly influenced by healthcare providers' recommendations [18], and recommendations from doctors and health workers emerge as key facilitators across studies, while providers in rural and semi-urban areas are often under-used as advocates [11]. In the national campaign, the trusted messengers are accredited social health activists (ASHAs), auxiliary nurse midwives (ANMs), medical officers, school teachers, and teams of the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram. In the Rajasthan study, health workers were willing to support vaccination but reported gaps in their confidence and preparedness for counselling families [24]. Their knowledge, confidence, and willingness to recommend the vaccine have received far less research attention than those of parents. Community Norms and Leaders Social norms within communities, including religious and cultural beliefs, influence acceptance in both directions [11,17]. In a structural equation model based on 1,609 parents of schoolgirls in Mysore district surveyed in 2010 and 2011, 78% stated an intention to vaccinate their daughters; perceived benefits increased intention, perceived barriers reduced it, and religion moderated the influence of social norms [17]. Engaging local leaders and using culturally adapted messages show promise, although most of this evidence comes from small studies in a limited number of districts. Motivation: willingness is not uptake Many Indian studies report moderate to high stated willingness to vaccinate daughters, particularly once parents receive information. In a quasi-experimental study of 70 parents recruited by convenience sampling in Manipur, for example, the proportion who said they would definitely vaccinate their daughter rose from 61.4% to 88.6% after three sessions of one-on-one health education [20]. A hospital-based contingent valuation study of 319 mothers in Haryana found that 79% were willing to pay for the vaccine, but their mean maximum willingness to pay (INR 629) was far below the market price of INR 2,000-3,000 per dose at the time [21]. These figures are not directly comparable, because the studies differ in setting, sampling, and the way acceptance was defined, and all of them describe stated willingness rather than vaccination. Two caveats therefore matter. First, expressed willingness in surveys often overstates actual uptake, and few Indian studies have followed parents from intention to vaccination. Second, timing matters to parents. In a survey of parents of 800 schoolgirls in Mysore, only 5.3% felt girls should be vaccinated at 10 years or younger, while 38.3% preferred 11-15 years, and a third did not know [16]. This suggests that the campaign's choice of 14 years, rather than the youngest eligible ages, may itself work in favour of parental acceptance. Practical issues: from cost to access and consent Before 2026, cost was among the most commonly reported practical barriers. HPV vaccines were available mainly in the private sector at prices out of reach for most families, and parents also cited lost work time to attend vaccination [11,18]. Economic evaluation from Punjab had shown that HPV vaccination of adolescent girls would be very cost-effective for the state and likely for other Indian states [27]. The national campaign has removed the cost barrier, so other practical issues now become more important. The first is reaching girls beyond schools. Girls who have dropped out of school are systematically harder to reach, and community perspectives from Uttar Pradesh underline the need for delivery models designed specifically for them [22]. The second is the experience of multi-age cohort delivery. Sikkim's 2018 statewide, school-based introduction for girls aged 9-13 years achieved more than 95% coverage with minimal refusal, a success attributed to political commitment, mandatory school enrolment, collaboration between health and education departments, and strong social mobilisation [7]. The third is the burden of consent and registration, because written parental consent, U-WIN registration, and facility-based sessions each add steps that can lose willing families. Table 2 summarises the drivers identified in Indian studies under each BeSD domain, together with their implications for the national campaign. What changes with the national campaign The national campaign alters the context of HPV vaccine decisions in three ways. It removes cost, the most consistently reported practical barrier. It carries the endorsement of the government and the immunisation programme, which may improve trust among parents who previously relied on private providers. title: Time trends of human papillomavirus-attributable head and neck cancers: the BROADEN study
abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is increasing in several Western countries, but this trend is less well understood in other geographical regions and for other head and neck cancers (HNC). The BROADEN (absolute BuRden Of HPV relAteD hEad and Neck) study assessed HPV-attributable fractions (HPV-AFs) of HNC including OPC in France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, China, and Japan over a 10-year period. Methods This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with HNC (oropharynx, oral cavity, nasopharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx cancer) in two time periods, 2008–2009 and 2018–2019. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the increasing incidence of HPV-driven oropharyngeal cancer in Western countries and its trends in other geographical regions and for other head and neck cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The BROADEN study assessed HPV-attributable fractions of head and neck cancers (HNC) including oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) in France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, China, and Japan over a 10-year period, using tissue samples from 6043 patients across 88 hospitals.
analysis.methods: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with HNC in two time periods, 2008–2009 and 2018–2019, and used formalin-fixed tissue samples tested centrally for HPV-DNA, HPV-E6*I mRNA, and p16INK4a immunohistochemistry.
analysis.main_results: Among 6043 patients, the HPV-AF in OPC increased across all countries, ranging from 0% in Portugal to 44.2% in Japan in 2008–2009, and from 20.0% to 51.7% in 2018–2019. Other HNC showed lower HPV-AF (≤5%) with no time trends.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the first and largest investigation to date on HPV causality and its time trends across five HNCs in seven countries, providing critical insights into geographic variation in HPV-AF.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results are essential for understanding time trends and geographic variation in HPV-attributable fractions, informing global strategies for the prevention and treatment of head and neck cancers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The increasing trend in HPV-AF for OPC reached statistical significance at 0.05 in all countries except China and Japan, indicating moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: The BROADEN study investigated the time trends of human papillomavirus (HPV)-attributable head and neck cancers (HNC) across seven countries over a 10-year period. It found that HPV-attributable fractions (HPV-AFs) for oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) increased in all countries, with Japan showing the highest HPV-AF. Other HNC types had lower HPV-AFs with no significant trends over time. The study is the first and largest to examine HPV causality and its geographic variation in multiple HNC subtypes, supporting the need for targeted prevention and treatment strategies. However, the statistical significance of the increasing trend was not observed in China and Japan, limiting the confidence in these findings. The results provide important insights for global HNC prevention and treatment planning.

elements_zh.methods: 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2008-2009 年和 2018-2019 年两个时期诊断为 HNC 的患者,并使用福尔马林固定的组织样本集中检测 HPV-DNA、HPV-E6*I mRNA 和 p16INK4a 免疫组织化学。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 6043 名患者中,所有国家 OPC 中的 HPV-AF 均有所增加,从 2008-2009 年葡萄牙的 0% 到日本的 44.2%,以及 2018-2019 年的 20.0% 到 51.7%。其他 HNC 显示较低的 HPV-AF (≤5%),无时间趋势。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the increasing incidence of HPV-driven oropharyngeal cancer in Western countries and its trends in other geographical regions and for other head and neck cancers.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The BROADEN study assessed HPV-attributable fractions of head and neck cancers (HNC) including oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) in France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, China, and Japan over a 10-year period, using tissue samples from 6043 patients across 88 hospitals.
analysis_en.methods: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with HNC in two time periods, 2008–2009 and 2018–2019, and used formalin-fixed tissue samples tested centrally for HPV-DNA, HPV-E6*I mRNA, and p16INK4a immunohistochemistry.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 6043 patients, the HPV-AF in OPC increased across all countries, ranging from 0% in Portugal to 44.2% in Japan in 2008–2009, and from 20.0% to 51.7% in 2018–2019. Other HNC showed lower HPV-AF (≤5%) with no time trends.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the first and largest investigation to date on HPV causality and its time trends across five HNCs in seven countries, providing critical insights into geographic variation in HPV-AF.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results are essential for understanding time trends and geographic variation in HPV-attributable fractions, informing global strategies for the prevention and treatment of head and neck cancers.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The increasing trend in HPV-AF for OPC reached statistical significance at 0.05 in all countries except China and Japan, indicating moderate confidence in the findings.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 归因的头颈癌的时间趋势:BROADEN 研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background The incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is increasing in several Western countries, but this trend is less well understood in other geographical regions and for other head and neck cancers (HNC). The BROADEN (absolute BuRden Of HPV relAteD hEad and Neck) study assessed HPV-attributable fractions (HPV-AFs) of HNC including OPC in France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain, China, and Japan over a 10-year period. Methods This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with HNC (oropharynx, oral cavity, nasopharynx, hypopharynx, and larynx cancer) in two time periods, 2008–2009 and 2018–2019. Formalin-fixed tissue samples were centrally tested for HPV-DNA, HPV-E6*I mRNA, and p16INK4a immunohistochemistry. HPV attributability required positive results in two of the three tests for OPC, and both HPV-DNA and HPV-E6*I mRNA positivity for other HNC. Results Among 6043 patients from 88 hospitals, the HPV-AF in OPC shown an increasing trend across all countries, with an HPV-AF ranging between 0% in Portugal and 44.2% in Japan in 2008-2009, and 20.0% and 51.7%, respectively, in 2018-2019. The increasing trend reached the statistical significance at 0.05 in all countries except China and Japan. Japan had the highest HPV-AF in 2008-2009. Other HNC showed lower HPV-AF (≤5%) with no time trends. Conclusion BROADEN is the first and largest study to date to investigate HPV causality and its time trends across five HNCs in seven countries. These results support the understanding of time trends and geographic variation in HPV-AF and are essential for global HNC prevention and treatment.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 发病率 或 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 驱动的口咽癌 (OPC) 在几个西方国家正在增加,但这种趋势在其他地理区域和其他头颈癌 (HNC) 中尚不清楚。BROADEN(HPV 相关头颈的绝对负担)研究评估了法国、德国、意大利、葡萄牙、西班牙、中国和日本的 HNC(包括 OPC)的 HPV 归因分数 (HPV-AF),历时 10 年。方法 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2008-2009 年和 2018-2019 年两个时期诊断为 HNC(口咽癌、口腔癌、鼻咽癌、下咽癌和喉癌)的患者。福尔马林固定的组织样本集中检测 HPV-DNA、HPV-E6*I mRNA 和 p16INK4a 免疫组织化学。HPV 归因要求 OPC 的三项测试中有两项呈阳性结果,而其他 HNC 的 HPV-DNA 和 HPV-E6*I mRNA 均呈阳性。结果 在来自 88 家医院的 6043 名患者中,OPC 中的 HPV-AF 在所有国家均呈上升趋势,2008-2009 年葡萄牙的 HPV-AF 为 0%,日本为 44.2%,2018-2019 年分别为 20.0% 和 51.7%。除中国和日本外,所有国家的增长趋势均达到0.05的统计显着性。2008-2009 年,日本的 HPV-AF 最高。其他 HNC 显示较低的 HPV-AF (≤5%),无时间趋势。结论 BROADEN 是迄今为止第一项也是规模最大的研究,旨在调查 7 个国家的 5 个 HNC 中 HPV 因果关系及其时间趋势。这些结果支持了解 HPV-AF 的时间趋势和地理变异,对于全球 HNC 预防和 治疗 至关重要。

title: Cross-protection and type-replacement over the 17 years after human papillomavirus vaccine introduction in young women
abstract: BACKGROUND: The study aim was to examine trends in non-4-valent and non-9-valent vaccine-type HPV detection over the first 17 years after U.S. HPV vaccine introduction among young women. METHODS: We recruited 13-26 year-old sexually experienced women (N = 2335) from hospital and community clinics for six surveillance studies from 2006 to 2023, with testing for HPV DNA by Roche Linear Array or TypeSeq2. Outcome variables were: 1) potentially carcinogenic alpha-9 and -7 non-vaccine-type HPV genetically related to HPV16 or 18 but not targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines (to assess for cross-protection) and 2) potentially carcinogenic alpha-5, -6, and - 11 non-vaccine-type HPV not closely genetically related to types targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines (to assess for type replacement). We used inverse probability of treatment weighting with propensity score to balance between-wave differences in participant characteristics in prevalence estimates and in tests of linear trend using surveillance study as a continuous variable. RESULTS: Among all, vaccinated, and unvaccinated participants, there were no significant trends in the prevalence of at least 1 non-vaccine-type HPV genetically related to HPV16 and/or HPV18 but not targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines. Positivity for non-vaccine-type HPV genetically unrelated to types targeted by the 4- or 9-valent vaccines remained stable from 2006 to 2015 but increased from 2016 to 2023; the trend was significant for all groups. CONCLUSIONS: We did not find evidence for cross-protection against types not targeted by the 4-valent or 9-valent vaccines, but did find a signal for possible emerging type replacement.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines trends in non-4-valent and non-9-valent human papillomavirus (HPV) detection over 17 years post-vaccine introduction among young women. It evaluates cross-protection against non-targeted HPV types and potential type replacement. The research recruited 2335 sexually experienced women aged 13-26 from 2006 to 2023, using HPV DNA testing methods. Results showed no significant trends in prevalence of non-vaccine-type HPV related to HPV16 or 18, but a significant increase in non-vaccine-type HPV unrelated to vaccine-targeted types from 2016 to 2023. However, the observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in causal interpretations.

title: HPV16 E7-Containing Exosomes May Contribute to PD-L1 Expression in Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes of Cervical Cancer
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16) plays a major role in the development of cervical cancer (CC). Programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) is an important feature of the tumor immune microenvironment and may affect responses to immune checkpoint blockade. However, the relationship between the HPV16 E7 oncoprotein and PD-L1 expression in TILs remains unclear. Aim To investigate the presence of HPV16 E7 protein in exosomes from CC tissues and plasma, determine the association between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs, and explore whether E7-rich tumor-derived exosomes contribute to increased PD-L1 expression in TILs. Study design This study combined clinical observational analyses and in vitro experiments. Three CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, a 30-patient HPV16-positive cohort, and a 104-patient tissue microarray cohort were analyzed. In vitro experiments were conducted to further examine the potential relationship between exosomal E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs. Methods Blood and pathological samples from 30 patients with HPV16-positive CC, as well as culture fluid from the C33A and SiHa CC cell lines, were collected. Exosomes were isolated, and E7 protein expression was assessed. Bioinformatics analyses of CC single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were performed to evaluate CD274 mRNA expression in TILs. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to assess PD-L1 protein expression in TILs in the 30-patient cohort, while multiplex immunofluorescence was used to evaluate E7 and PD-L1 expression in TILs in a 104-patient tissue microarray. Exosome uptake by TILs was assessed using confocal microscopy. TILs were co-cultured with exosomes, and HPV16 E7 and PD-L1 expression was evaluated by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and western blotting in the TIL blank control, co-culture blank control, co-culture empty vector, and co-culture E7-overexpression groups. Results E7 protein was detected in exosomes from the peripheral blood of 28 of 30 patients (93.3%) and in exosomes from SiHa cell culture. PD-L1 was expressed in TILs, with a positive rate of 43.3% (13/30). In the tissue microarray cohort (n = 103; 28 events), higher CD3 + PD-L1 + /CD3 + expression was associated with poorer survival (HR = 2.97, p = 0.009). CD3 + E7 + /CD3 + expression showed a borderline association with poorer survival in the dichotomized analysis (HR = 2.15, p = 0.052) but was significantly associated with survival when modeled as a continuous variable (per 10%: HR = 1.28, p = 0.002). In the 30-patient cohort, exosomal E7 protein content was significantly associated with PD-L1 expression in TILs (Cramér's V = 0.728, p = 0.0001). qRT-PCR and western blotting demonstrated increased PD-L1 mRNA and protein expression in TILs exposed to exosomes from E7-overexpressing cells. Conclusion HPV16 E7 protein is present in exosomes from patients with CC and HPV16-positive CC cells. Higher exosomal E7 levels are associated with increased PD-L1 expression in TILs, and exposure to E7-rich exosomes is associated with upregulated PD-L1 expression in TILs. These findings suggest that exosomal E7 may contribute to PD-L1 regulation in TILs and may be associated with poorer prognosis in patients with CC. Further studies are needed to determine whether E7 directly mediates this effect and to clarify its functional and clinical significance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景 人乳头瘤病毒 16 (HPV16) 在 宫颈癌 (CC) 的发展中发挥着重要作用。HPV16 E7 癌蛋白与肿瘤浸润淋巴细胞 (TIL) 中 PD-L1 表达之间的关系仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究结合了临床观察分析和体外实验。对三个 宫颈癌 单细胞 RNA 测序数据集、30 例 HPV16 阳性 队列研究 和 104 例患者组织微阵列 队列研究 进行了分析。
elements_zh.methods: 收集了 30 名 HPV16 阳性 宫颈癌 患者的血液和病理样本,以及 C33A 和 SiHa 宫颈癌 细胞系的培养液。分离外泌体,并评估 E7 蛋白表达。使用免疫组织化学 (IHC) 评估 30 名患者 队列研究 中 TIL 中的 PD-L1 蛋白表达,同时使用多重免疫荧光评估 104 名患者组织微阵列中 TIL 中 E7 和 PD-L1 的表达。使用共聚焦显微镜评估 TIL 对外泌体的摄取。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 30 名患者中 28 名 (93.3%) 的外泌体和 SiHa 细胞培养物的外泌体中检测到 E7 蛋白。在组织微阵列 队列研究(n = 103;28 个事件)中,较高的 CD3 + PD-L1 + /CD3 + 表达与较差的生存率相关(HR = 2.97,p = 0.009)。在二分分析中,CD3 + E7 + /CD3 + 表达与较差的生存率呈边缘相关(HR = 2.15,p = 0.052),但当建模为连续变量时,与生存率显着相关(每 10%:HR = 1.28,p = 0.002)。在 30 名患者的 队列研究 中,外泌体 E7 蛋白含量与 TIL 中的 PD-L1 表达显着相关(Cramér V = 0.728,p = 0.0001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,外泌体 E7 可能有助于 TIL 中的 PD-L1 调节,并可能与 宫颈癌 患者较差的预后相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为 HPV16 阳性 宫颈癌 的靶向治疗的开发提供信息,并提高对这种情况下免疫检查点阻断反应的理解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 需要进一步的研究来确定 E7 是否直接介导这种作用并阐明其功能和临床意义。由于该研究的观察性质以及需要额外的机制验证,证据强度适中。

title: Knowledge, attitudes and human papillomavirus vaccine recommendation practices among primary care physicians in Bahrain: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Physician recommendation is one of the main determinants of HPV vaccine uptake, yet little is known about how often primary care physicians in Bahrain recommend the vaccine. We assessed their knowledge, attitudes and recommendation practices and looked for factors associated with regular recommendation. Methods We surveyed 205 physicians working in primary health care centres in all four governorates of Bahrain in 2025. A self-administered questionnaire covered knowledge (24 items), attitudes (6 items), confidence, and how often the physician had recommended the vaccine in the previous six months. Regular recommendation (about once a month or more) was the outcome, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors. Results The mean knowledge score was 19.1 of 24 (SD 2.8). Most physicians considered the vaccine safe (81.0%) and effective (88.8%), and 77.6% supported its place in the routine schedule. Far fewer perceived that parents will accept it (28.8%) or that the community would (36.1%). In the previous six months, 35.6% had never recommended the vaccine, 28.3% had done so once or twice, and 36.1% recommended it regularly. Regular recommendation was associated with more than four years of experience (5–15 years: aOR 5.34, 95% CI 2.39–11.93; over 15 years: aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.15–12.35) and with higher perceived parental and community acceptance (aOR 1.33 per point, 95% CI 1.07–1.65). Knowledge was not associated with recommendation (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 0.92–1.18). Conclusions Primary care physicians in Bahrain have good knowledge of HPV vaccination and view the vaccine favourably. Because the vaccine is delivered through school campaigns, physicians have few routine opportunities to recommend it, and their role is mainly counselling hesitant parents. Recommendation was linked to experience and to what physicians expect parents to accept, not to knowledge. Training for early-career physicians and feedback on actual parental acceptance may help.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Physician recommendation is a key determinant of HPV vaccine uptake, yet there is limited understanding of how frequently primary care physicians in Bahrain recommend the vaccine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 205 primary care physicians working in primary health care centres across all four governorates of Bahrain.

title_zh: 巴林初级保健医生的知识、态度和 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗 推荐实践:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Physician recommendation is one of the main determinants of HPV vaccine uptake, yet little is known about how often primary care physicians in Bahrain recommend the vaccine. We assessed their knowledge, attitudes and recommendation practices and looked for factors associated with regular recommendation. Methods We surveyed 205 physicians working in primary health care centres in all four governorates of Bahrain in 2025. A self-administered questionnaire covered knowledge (24 items), attitudes (6 items), confidence, and how often the physician had recommended the vaccine in the previous six months. Regular recommendation (about once a month or more) was the outcome, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors. Results The mean knowledge score was 19.1 of 24 (SD 2.8). Most physicians considered the vaccine safe (81.0%) and effective (88.8%), and 77.6% supported its place in the routine schedule. Far fewer perceived that parents will accept it (28.8%) or that the community would (36.1%). In the previous six months, 35.6% had never recommended the vaccine, 28.3% had done so once or twice, and 36.1% recommended it regularly. Regular recommendation was associated with more than four years of experience (5–15 years: aOR 5.34, 95% CI 2.39–11.93; over 15 years: aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.15–12.35) and with higher perceived parental and community acceptance (aOR 1.33 per point, 95% CI 1.07–1.65). Knowledge was not associated with recommendation (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 0.92–1.18). Conclusions Primary care physicians in Bahrain have good knowledge of HPV vaccination and view the vaccine favourably. Because the vaccine is delivered through school campaigns, physicians have few routine opportunities to recommend it, and their role is mainly counselling hesitant parents. Recommendation was linked to experience and to what physicians expect parents to accept, not to knowledge. Training for early-career physicians and feedback on actual parental acceptance may help.

title: Knowledge, attitudes and acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccination among parents in Bahrain: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Bahrain introduced human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination for adolescent girls and boys through school campaigns in October 2023. Parents' decisions are central to uptake, yet their views have not been studied in Bahrain. We assessed parents' knowledge, attitudes and acceptance of the vaccine and the factors associated with willingness to vaccinate. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, interviewer-administered survey between July and September 2025 in four governmental primary health care centres, one randomly selected from each governorate. Bahraini parents of children aged 6 to 14 years were recruited by convenience sampling after their consultation. The questionnaire covered sociodemographic characteristics, a 20-item knowledge score (for parents aware of the vaccine), eight attitude statements forming vaccine-confidence and vaccine-concern subscales, acceptance when offered, and willingness if offered. We used chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 368 parents, 74.0% were mothers and 62.9% had a university education. Most knew that HPV affects women (83.1%) and causes cervical cancer (72.1%), but only 46.2% had heard of the vaccine. Just 22.0% had been offered it for a child, and 70.0% of those (56/80) accepted. Among the 285 parents not yet offered it, 60.4% were willing. In all, 80.6% said a recommendation from doctors and nurses would encourage them, and 54.6% said fear of side effects discouraged them. Willingness was 84.8% with positive and 37.9% with negative attitudes; vaccine confidence (adjusted OR 5.8 per SD, 95% CI 3.5–9.8) and fewer vaccine concerns (2.4, 1.7–3.6) independently predicted willingness. Among parents aware of the vaccine, mean knowledge was 14.0/20 (SD 3.9); willingness was 83.7% with good knowledge versus 57.1–58.1% otherwise (p = 0.017), but knowledge was not independently associated once attitude was included (adjusted OR 1.12 per point, 95% CI 0.94–1.33). Positive attitudes were more common among health-sector workers (74.5% vs 45.1–48.1%; p = 0.002). Conclusion Most parents in Bahrain are open to HPV vaccination, but awareness of the vaccine is low and concerns about side effects are common. Attitude, more than knowledge, distinguished parents who were willing to vaccinate. Recommendation by doctors and nurses, together with clear information about vaccine safety, is a practical way to turn openness into acceptance.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Bahrain assessed parents' knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. The study found that most parents were open to vaccinating their children, but awareness of the vaccine was low, and concerns about side effects were common. Positive attitudes were more prevalent among health-sector workers, and vaccine confidence and fewer concerns independently predicted willingness to vaccinate. The findings highlight the importance of physician recommendations and clear safety information in increasing HPV vaccination acceptance. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and convenience sampling limits the confidence in the results, making the evidence moderate.

title_zh: 巴林家长对 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 的知识、态度和接受度:一项横断面研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Bahrain introduced human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination for adolescent girls and boys through school campaigns in October 2023. Parents' decisions are central to uptake, yet their views have not been studied in Bahrain. We assessed parents' knowledge, attitudes and acceptance of the vaccine and the factors associated with willingness to vaccinate. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, interviewer-administered survey between July and September 2025 in four governmental primary health care centres, one randomly selected from each governorate. Bahraini parents of children aged 6 to 14 years were recruited by convenience sampling after their consultation. The questionnaire covered sociodemographic characteristics, a 20-item knowledge score (for parents aware of the vaccine), eight attitude statements forming vaccine-confidence and vaccine-concern subscales, acceptance when offered, and willingness if offered. We used chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 368 parents, 74.0% were mothers and 62.9% had a university education. Most knew that HPV affects women (83.1%) and causes cervical cancer (72.1%), but only 46.2% had heard of the vaccine. Just 22.0% had been offered it for a child, and 70.0% of those (56/80) accepted. Among the 285 parents not yet offered it, 60.4% were willing. In all, 80.6% said a recommendation from doctors and nurses would encourage them, and 54.6% said fear of side effects discouraged them. Willingness was 84.8% with positive and 37.9% with negative attitudes; vaccine confidence (adjusted OR 5.8 per SD, 95% CI 3.5–9.8) and fewer vaccine concerns (2.4, 1.7–3.6) independently predicted willingness. Among parents aware of the vaccine, mean knowledge was 14.0/20 (SD 3.9); willingness was 83.7% with good knowledge versus 57.1–58.1% otherwise (p = 0.017), but knowledge was not independently associated once attitude was included (adjusted OR 1.12 per point, 95% CI 0.94–1.33). Positive attitudes were more common among health-sector workers (74.5% vs 45.1–48.1%; p = 0.002). Conclusion Most parents in Bahrain are open to HPV vaccination, but awareness of the vaccine is low and concerns about side effects are common. Attitude, more than knowledge, distinguished parents who were willing to vaccinate. Recommendation by doctors and nurses, together with clear information about vaccine safety, is a practical way to turn openness into acceptance.

title: HPV-Associated Tonsillar Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Oral High-Risk HPV mRNA as a Candidate Biomarker
abstract: ABSTRACT Early detection of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal cancer is an unmet need, as its premalignant lesions remain unestablished. We hypothesized that such lesions exist in individuals with oral high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) mRNA. We preoperatively screened 1,180 individuals undergoing tonsillectomy due to benign conditions and detected five with oral HR-HPV mRNA. Serial sectioning of the entire excised tonsils identified HPV-associated intraepithelial lesions in three of these five individuals. A similar lesion was identified in an additional individual with oral HPV16 infection with unknown oral HR-HPV mRNA status. Intraepithelial lesions in two individuals were HPV16-associated and showed moderate-to-severe atypia, whereas those in the other two individuals were associated with other HR-HPV and showed minimal-to-mild atypia. Based on HPV life cycle, the former were classified as transforming lesions and the latter as productive-to-intermediate lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed molecular profiles intermediate between those of normal epithelium and HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. These findings establish the first evidence for HPV-associated tonsillar premalignant lesions and suggest oral HR-HPV mRNA as a candidate biomarker.

title: The assembly pathway for human papillomavirus L1 capsid protein is encoded in electrostatic interactions.
abstract: Human papillomavirus L1 protein spontaneously folds and assembles into 60 nm virus-like particles (VLP), with T = 7d icosahedral symmetry at high salt concentrations but not in low salt. Rapid increase from low to high salt during the assembly process gives poor-quality VLPs, while slowly increasing salt, over as many as 48 h, gives rise to high-quality VLPs. Insight into this behavior is drawn from a computational model based on the cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the human papillomavirus Type 16 VLP. Electrostatic potential energy barriers were calculated using the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation. After initial, rapid oligomerization of monomers into symmetrical pentamers (capsomeres), these units form pairwise interactions in energetic order, lowest barrier first. But at high salt concentrations, the energetic barriers are more or less equal and irregular particles form, both in simulation and in experiments. The interaction interfaces were modified by mutation to favor the smaller, 30 nm T = 1 icosahedral symmetry and disfavor T = 7d symmetry. The results were smaller particles. By carefully controlling ionic strength, and/or by mutating interface residues by design, it is possible to make high quality, highly immunogenic VLPs directly from unpurified bacterial lysate, without requiring the use of a disassembly/reassembly step.

Insight into this behavior is drawn from a computational model based on the cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the human papillomavirus Type 16 VLP. Electrostatic potential energy barriers were calculated using the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann equation. After initial, rapid oligomerization of monomers into symmetrical pentamers (capsomeres), these units form pairwise interactions in energetic order, lowest barrier first. But at high salt concentrations, the energetic barriers are more or less equal and irregular particles form, both in simulation and in experiments. The interaction interfaces were modified by mutation to favor the smaller, 30 nm T = 1 icosahedral symmetry and disfavor T = 7d symmetry. The results were smaller particles. By carefully controlling ionic strength, and/or by mutating interface residues by design, it is possible to make high quality, highly immunogenic VLPs directly from unpurified bacterial lysate, without requiring the use of a disassembly/reassembly step.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the assembly pathway of human papillomavirus (HPV) L1 capsid protein, revealing that salt concentration significantly influences the formation of virus-like particles (VLPs) with specific icosahedral symmetries. High salt concentrations lead to irregular VLPs due to equal energetic barriers, while slow salt increase produces high-quality VLPs. Computational modeling based on cryo-EM data of HPV16 VLPs was used to analyze the process, and mutation of interaction interfaces was shown to favor T = 1 symmetry. These findings suggest that controlling ionic strength or modifying residues can enhance VLP quality for vaccine development. abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 L1 蛋白自发折叠并组装成 60 nm 病毒样颗粒 (VLP),在高盐浓度下具有 T = 7d 二十面体对称性,但在低盐浓度下则不然。在组装过程中从低盐到高盐的快速增加会产生质量较差的 VLP,而在长达 48 小时内缓慢增加盐会产生高质量的 VLP。对这种行为的深入了解是通过基于 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 VLP 低温电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构的计算模型得出的。使用线性化泊松-玻尔兹曼方程计算静电势能垒。在单体最初快速寡聚成对称五聚体(壳粒)后,这些单元以能量顺序形成成对相互作用,最低势垒首先。但在高盐浓度下,无论是在模拟还是在实验中,能量势垒或多或少都是相等的,并且粒子形式不规则。相互作用界面由 突变 修改,以支持更小的 30 nm T = 1 二十面体对称性,而不支持 T = 7d 对称性。结果是更小的颗粒。通过仔细控制离子强度和/或通过设计突变界面残基,可以直接从未纯化的细菌裂解物中制备高质量、高免疫原性的VLP,而不需要使用拆卸/重新组装步骤。

title: Predicting high-risk HPV infection and genotype co-infection using genital tract microecological and pathogen characteristics: a machine learning study
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract co-infections may influence HR-HPV acquisition, clearance, and persistence. However, quantitative prediction models integrating vaginal microecological indicators, genital tract pathogens, and HR-HPV genotype co-infection patterns remain limited. Methods This retrospective study included 3,403 patients who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and genital tract pathogen testing at the gynecology outpatient clinic of Hainan Women and Children’s Medical Center between January 2022 and December 2025. Of these, 765 were HR-HPV-positive and 2,638 were HR-HPV-negative. Candidate predictors were selected using univariable analysis, multicollinearity assessment based on the variance inflation factor (VIF ≦ 4), and the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with 10-fold cross-validation within the training set. Classifier chains (C ≦ C) and ensemble classifier chains (ECC) were applied to the multi-label prediction of HR-HPV genotypes. Model predictions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). title: A Wider Screening of High-Risk Oncogenic Human Papillomaviruses in Cameroon Calls for An Optimized Generation of Vaccine-Clade Coverage
abstract: Abstract Background: High-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HR-HPV) are unevenly distributed worldwide, which may affect the effectiveness of current prophylactic vaccines. We assessed the molecular epidemiology of HR-HPV among Cameroonian women and its adequacy with existing vaccine valence. Methods: Sexually active, unvaccinated women aged 18 years or older were enrolled between June 2020 and May 2022 in two reference hospitals in Yaoundé and Douala, Cameroon. Cervical samples were screened for HR-HPV by real-time PCR, genotyped using a second real-time PCR platform, and discordant or uninterpretable results were confirmed with a third multiplex real-time PCR assay. Logistic regression identified factors associated with HR-HPV positivity. Results: Of 413 women enrolled (median age 40 years, interquartile range 33 to 49), 96 (23.2%, 95% confidence interval 17.2 to 25.6) tested positive for HR-HPV. Thirteen genotypes were identified, most frequently HPV18 (19.8%), HPV16 (16.7%), HPV58 (16.7%), HPV39 (15.6%), HPV66 (13.5%), and HPV59 (12.5%). Multiple-genotype infections were detected in 37.5% of positive samples, ranging from two to five genotypes per specimen. Cytological abnormalities were observed in 70 women (17%), mostly low-grade lesions. First sexual intercourse before age 15, more than three lifetime sexual partners, and the presence of cervical lesions were significantly associated with HR-HPV positivity. Conclusion: HR-HPV infection is common among Cameroonian women, with wide genotypic diversity and frequent multiple infections. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular epidemiology of high-risk oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HR-HPV) among Cameroonian women, highlighting the prevalence of HR-HPV infections and the diversity of genotypes. The research aimed to evaluate the adequacy of current vaccine valence in this population. The study's findings underscore the importance of continued cervical cancer screening programs in the region. analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HR-HPV感染在喀麦隆女性中很常见,具有广泛的基因型多样性和频繁的多重感染。非 疫苗 基因型(例如 HPV39、HPV59 和 HPV66)是最常见的,这种模式可能需要在这种情况下考虑更广价的 HPV 疫苗。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了喀麦隆对广价 HPV 疫苗 的需求,并强调了继续投资 宫颈癌 筛查计划的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注未接种疫苗的女性以及依赖宫颈样本,而宫颈样本可能无法完全代表人群。由于该研究的观察性质,证据的强度中等。

title: Prevalence, HPV Type Categories, and Associated Factors of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection among Women in Mzuzu City, Malawi
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, which remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Malawi. Understanding the local distribution of HPV types and their associated risk factors is essential for optimising screening and vaccination strategies. The study aimed to establish the distribution of HPV types circulating among women in Mzuzu, Malawi. This was a cross-sectional retrospective study which included 385 women attending gynecological services at Mzuzu Urban Health Centre, Malawi, between May 2021 and December 2022. Clinical records were reviewed for age, residential location, HIV status, and HPV results. HPV DNA detection and genotyping were performed using the Xpert HPV assay, which identifies HPV 16, HPV 18/45, and a pooled group of 11 other high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes. Descriptive statistics were used to assess the prevalence of high-risk HPV and its type distribution. The overall prevalence of HR- HPV infection was 42.9%. The predominant types were among the other HR-HPV types (34%), followed by HPV 18/45 (11.7%) and HPV 16 (9.1%). Multiple infections occurred in 26.7% of positive cases, with the most common combination being HPV 18/45 and other HR-HPV types. The highest infection rate was observed among women less than 26 years (55.6%), while Mzuzu South recorded the largest number of HPV-positive cases (49.2%). HPV infection was more frequent among HIV-positive women (51.6%) than HIV-negative women (40%). The study demonstrates a high prevalence and diversity of HR-HPV type categories among women in Mzuzu City, with non-vaccine HR-HPV types predominating and a notable association with HIV infection. These findings emphasise the need for ongoing molecular surveillance and the consideration of broader-spectrum HPV vaccines. Integrating HPV screening into HIV care and prioritising preventive interventions for younger women may substantially reduce the cervical cancer burden in Malawi.
journal: Journal of Epidemiology and Global Health

Conducted as a cross-sectional retrospective study between May 2021 and December 2022, it included 385 women attending gynecological services. The Xpert HPV assay was used to detect and genotype HPV, identifying HPV 16, HPV 18/45, and 11 other HR-HPV types. HIV-positive women had a higher infection rate (51.6%) compared to HIV-negative women (40%). elements_zh.scope_and_question: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 的主要原因,这仍然是撒哈拉以南非洲地区,特别是马拉维的一个重大公共卫生挑战。该研究旨在确定马拉维姆祖祖女性中流行的 HPV 类型的分布情况。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项横断面回顾性研究,纳入了 2021 年 5 月至 2022 年 12 月期间在马拉维姆祖祖城市卫生中心接受妇科服务的 385 名女性。对临床记录的年龄、居住地点、艾滋病毒状况和 HPV 结果进行了审查。使用 Xpert HPV 检测进行 HPV DNA 检测和基因分型,该检测可识别 HPV 16、HPV 18/45 以及其他 11 种 高危型HPV (HR-HPV) 基因型的汇总组。使用描述性统计来评估 高危型HPV 的 患病率 及其类型分布。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HR-HPV感染的总体患病率为42.9%。主要类型是其他 HR-HPV 类型 (34%),其次是 HPV 18/45 (11.7%) 和 HPV 16 (9.1%)。26.7% 的阳性病例发生多重感染,最常见的组合是 HPV 18/45 和其他 HR-HPV 类型。该研究表明,姆祖祖市女性的 HR-HPV 类型类别具有较高的 患病率 和多样性,其中非 疫苗 HR-HPV 类型占主导地位,并且与 HIV 感染存在显着关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有报告 HPV 感染或其进展为 宫颈癌 的具体机制。它还没有解决非 疫苗 HR-HPV 类型对疾病结果的潜在影响或当前针对这些类型的筛查方法的有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现强调了对持续分子 监测 的需求以及对更广谱 HPV 疫苗 的考虑。将 HPV 筛查纳入艾滋病毒护理并优先考虑对年轻女性进行预防性干预可能会大大减轻马拉维的 宫颈癌 负担。

title_zh: 马拉维姆祖祖市女性 患病率、HPV 类型类别以及高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 感染的相关因素
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, which remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Malawi. The study aimed to establish the distribution of HPV types circulating among women in Mzuzu, Malawi. This was a cross-sectional retrospective study which included 385 women attending gynecological services at Mzuzu Urban Health Centre, Malawi, between May 2021 and December 2022. Clinical records were reviewed for age, residential location, HIV status, and HPV results. HPV DNA detection and genotyping were performed using the Xpert HPV assay, which identifies HPV 16, HPV 18/45, and a pooled group of 11 other high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes. These findings emphasise the need for ongoing molecular surveillance and the consideration of broader-spectrum HPV vaccines. Integrating HPV screening into HIV care and prioritising preventive interventions for younger women may substantially reduce the cervical cancer burden in Malawi.

title: Prevalence of High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Infection in Pregnant Women and Its Association with Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is common among women of reproductive age, but data on HPV infection during pregnancy in South-East Asia remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of high-risk HPV infection and abnormal cervical cytology among pregnant women in Thailand, identify factors associated with high-risk HPV infection, and explore its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Methods This cross-sectional study included pregnant women aged ≥ 18 years attending antenatal care at a tertiary referral hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, between June 2024 and May 2025. Cervical samples were tested for 14 high-risk HPV genotypes using real-time polymerase chain reaction and assessed by liquid-based cytology. Demographic, reproductive, and epidemiological characteristics were collected using questionnaires and electronic medical records. Pregnancy outcomes were recorded after delivery. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with high-risk HPV infection. Results Among 255 participants, 40 tested positive for high-risk HPV, giving a prevalence of 15.7% (95% CI 11.5–20.7). Other high-risk HPV genotypes were most common (12.2%), followed by HPV 16 (3.9%) and HPV 18 (1.6%). Abnormal cervical cytology was detected in 2.0% of participants (four ASC-US and one HSIL). Younger age and having three or more lifetime sexual partners were independently associated with high-risk HPV infection. Pregnancy outcome data were available for 216 participants. No statistically significant associations were observed between high-risk HPV infection and abortion, preterm delivery, preterm premature rupture of membranes, fetal growth restriction, low birth weight, gestational hypertension, or pre-eclampsia. Conclusions High-risk HPV infection was identified in 15.7% of pregnant women, while abnormal cervical cytology was uncommon and most high-risk HPV infections occurred in women with normal cytology. Antenatal care may provide an opportunity to improve cervical cancer screening coverage. No significant association between high-risk HPV infection and adverse pregnancy outcomes was observed, although the study was not powered primarily to assess these outcomes.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染在育龄妇女中很常见,但东南亚妊娠期 HPV 感染的数据仍然有限。本研究旨在确定泰国孕妇中高危型HPV感染和宫颈细胞学异常的患病率,确定与高危型HPV感染相关的因素,并探讨其与不良妊娠结局的关系。方法 这项横断面研究纳入了 2024 年 6 月至 2025 年 5 月期间在泰国曼谷一家三级转诊医院接受产前护理的年龄≥ 18 岁的孕妇。使用实时聚合酶链反应检测宫颈样本的 14 种 高危型HPV 基因型,并通过液基细胞学进行评估。使用问卷和电子病历收集人口统计、生殖和流行病学特征。分娩后记录妊娠结局。使用逻辑回归来识别与 高危型HPV 感染相关的因素。结果 在 255 名参与者中,40 名 高危型HPV 检测呈阳性,患病率 为 15.7% (95% CI 11.5–20.7)。其他 高危型HPV 基因型最常见 (12.2%),其次是 HPV 16 (3.9%) 和 HPV 18 (1.6%)。2.0% 的参与者(4 名 ASC-US 和 1 名 HSIL)检测到宫颈细胞学异常。年龄较小和一生拥有三个或以上性伴侣与 高危型HPV 感染独立相关。216 名参与者的妊娠结果数据可用。高危型HPV 感染与流产、早产、胎膜早破、胎儿生长受限、低出生体重、妊娠期高血压或先兆子痫之间没有观察到统计学上显着的关联。结论 15.7%的孕妇中发现高危型HPV感染,而宫颈细胞学异常并不常见,大多数高危型HPV感染发生在细胞学正常的女性中。产前护理可能提供提高 宫颈癌 筛查覆盖率的机会。尽管该研究的主要目的不是评估这些结果,但没有观察到 高危型HPV 感染与不良妊娠结局之间存在显着关联。

title: Arginine vasopressin deficiency following 9-valent human papillomavirus vaccination: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and associated diseases are a major global health burden, and the 9-valent HPV vaccine is widely used to reduce their incidence and mortality. This study reports the first documented case of arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency following 9-valent HPV vaccination, to highlight the need for clinical vigilance for potential post-vaccination adverse events. Case presentation A 30-year-old Chinese woman developed symptoms after her first dose of the 9-valent HPV vaccine in July 2023. This report details her clinical data, laboratory results, MRI findings, treatment, and follow-up outcomes. One day after vaccination, the patient developed polyuria and severe thirst, with no prior history of head trauma, peripartum events, or endocrine disorders. Laboratory tests confirmed AVP deficiency, and brain MRI showed pituitary stalk thickening and absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot, consistent with infundibulo-neurohypophysitis. Following treatment with desmopressin, her polyuria and polydipsia were well controlled. At 30 months of follow-up, the desmopressin dose had been reduced to 0.025 mg twice daily without symptom recurrence, and repeat MRI showed normalized pituitary morphology. Conclusion This is the first reported case of AVP deficiency possibly associated with 9-valent HPV vaccination. Although causality cannot be established from a single case, clinicians should be aware of new-onset polyuria and polydipsia after vaccination and consider AVP deficiency in the differential diagnosis.

title_zh: 9 价 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 后精氨酸加压素缺乏:病例报告
source_body_en: Abstract Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and associated diseases are a major global health burden, and the 9-valent HPV vaccine is widely used to reduce their incidence and mortality. This study reports the first documented case of arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency following 9-valent HPV vaccination, to highlight the need for clinical vigilance for potential post-vaccination adverse events. Case presentation A 30-year-old Chinese woman developed symptoms after her first dose of the 9-valent HPV vaccine in July 2023. This report details her clinical data, laboratory results, MRI findings, treatment, and follow-up outcomes. One day after vaccination, the patient developed polyuria and severe thirst, with no prior history of head trauma, peripartum events, or endocrine disorders. Laboratory tests confirmed AVP deficiency, and brain MRI showed pituitary stalk thickening and absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot, consistent with infundibulo-neurohypophysitis. Following treatment with desmopressin, her polyuria and polydipsia were well controlled. At 30 months of follow-up, the desmopressin dose had been reduced to 0.025 mg twice daily without symptom recurrence, and repeat MRI showed normalized pituitary morphology. Conclusion This is the first reported case of AVP deficiency possibly associated with 9-valent HPV vaccination. Although causality cannot be established from a single case, clinicians should be aware of new-onset polyuria and polydipsia after vaccination and consider AVP deficiency in the differential diagnosis.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染及相关疾病是全球主要的健康负担,9 价 HPV 疫苗 被广泛用于减少其 发病率 和 死亡率。本研究报告了首例有记录的 9 价 HPV 疫苗接种 后精氨酸加压素 (AVP) 缺乏的病例,以强调临床对 疫苗接种 后潜在不良事件保持警惕的必要性。病例介绍 一名 30 岁的中国女性于 2023 年 7 月首次接种 9 价 HPV 疫苗 后出现症状。本报告详细介绍了她的临床数据、实验室结果、MRI 结果、治疗 和随访结果。疫苗接种后一天,患者出现多尿和严重口渴,既往无头部外伤、围产期事件或内分泌紊乱病史。实验室检查证实 AVP 缺乏,脑 MRI 显示垂体柄增厚且缺乏垂体后亮点,与漏斗部神经垂体炎一致。治疗服用去氨加压素后,她的多尿和多饮得到了很好的控制。在 30 个月的随访中,去氨加压素剂量已减少至 0.025 mg,每天两次,没有症状复发,重复 MRI 显示垂体形态正常化。结论 这是首例报道的 AVP 缺陷可能与 9 价 HPV 疫苗接种 相关。虽然不能从单一病例中确定因果关系,但临床医生应注意 疫苗接种 后新发的多尿和多饮,并在鉴别 诊断 时考虑 AVP 缺乏。

title: Mathematical Modeling and Stability Analysis of Human Papillomavirus Transmission and Cervical Cancer Progression with Vaccination and Treatment
abstract: In this study, we develop and analyze a deterministic mathematical model, the Human Papillomavirus–Cervical Cancer Transmission and Control Model (HPV-CCT-CM), to investigate the transmission dynamics of HPV leading to cervical cancer under the combined effects of vaccination and treatment interventions. The model extends existing frameworks by incorporating compartments for susceptible, vaccinated, infected, precancerous, cancerous, treated, and recovered females, as well as susceptible, infected, and recovered males, with clinical interventions explicitly represented. We establish the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium states and analyze their stability properties. The basic reproduction number, R0, and the associated stability conditions are examined. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for R0 1. Numerical results demonstrate that the endemic equilibrium remains stable even when the effective contact rate is above 0.7 and becomes unstable when the contact rate exceeds 1.0. These findings indicate that controlling HPV transmission and cervical cancer requires reducing contact rates while enhancing vaccination coverage, vaccine efficacy, and access to treatment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the transmission dynamics of human papillomavirus (HPV) leading to cervical cancer under the combined effects of vaccination and treatment interventions. The research is motivated by the need to understand how these interventions can influence the spread of HPV and the progression to cervical cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A deterministic mathematical model, the HPV-CCT-CM, was developed and analyzed to study the transmission dynamics of HPV and cervical cancer progression. The model incorporates compartments for susceptible, vaccinated, infected, precancerous, cancerous, treated, and recovered females, as well as susceptible, infected, and recovered males.
analysis.methods: The model was analyzed to establish the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium states and to examine their stability properties. The basic reproduction number, R0, and the associated stability conditions were also analyzed.
analysis.main_results: The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for R0 < 1. Numerical results demonstrate that the endemic equilibrium remains stable even when the effective contact rate is above 0.7 and becomes unstable when the contact rate exceeds 1.0.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that controlling HPV transmission and cervical cancer requires reducing contact rates while enhancing vaccination coverage, vaccine efficacy, and access to treatment. This study provides novel insights into the stability of equilibrium states under varying contact rates and intervention strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for HPV surveillance, prevention, and control by highlighting the importance of reducing contact rates and improving vaccination and treatment programs. They also contribute to the understanding of how mathematical models can be used to predict and manage HPV-related diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a deterministic mathematical model and does not account for real-world variability or data from clinical trials. The evidence is derived from theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, which may have limitations in capturing complex biological interactions. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the evidence and the reliance on model-based results.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a deterministic mathematical model, the HPV-CCT-CM, to investigate the transmission dynamics of human papillomavirus (HPV) and its progression to cervical cancer under vaccination and treatment interventions. The model includes compartments for different stages of infection and disease in both males and females. The research establishes the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium states and analyzes their stability. The disease-free equilibrium is stable for R0 < 1, while the endemic equilibrium remains stable at contact rates above 0.7 but becomes unstable when contact rates exceed 1.0. The authors interpret that reducing contact rates and enhancing vaccination and treatment coverage are essential for controlling HPV transmission and cervical cancer. These findings have implications for public health strategies in HPV surveillance and prevention. However, the study is limited to theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, which may not fully capture real-world complexities. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the abstract-only nature of the study and the reliance on model-based results.
