elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨在疫苗接种和治疗干预措施的联合作用下,人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)导致宫颈癌的传播动态。这项研究的动机是需要了解这些干预措施如何影响 HPV 的传播和 宫颈癌 的进展。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开发并分析了确定性数学模型 HPV-CCT-CM,以研究 HPV 的 传播 动态和 宫颈癌 进展。该模型包含易感、疫苗接种、感染、癌前、癌变、治疗和康复女性以及易感、感染和康复男性的隔间。
elements_zh.methods: 分析该模型以确定无病和地方性平衡状态的存在并检查其稳定性。还分析了基本再生数 R0 和相关的稳定性条件。
elements_zh.main_results: 当 R0 < 1 时,无病平衡是局部渐近稳定的。数值结果表明,即使有效接触率高于 0.7,地方性平衡也保持稳定,而当接触率超过 1.0 时,地方性平衡就会变得不稳定。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,控制 HPV 传播 和 宫颈癌 需要降低接触率,同时提高 疫苗接种 覆盖率、疫苗 功效和 治疗 的可及性。这项研究为不同接触率和干预策略下平衡状态的稳定性提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调降低接触率和改进 疫苗接种 和 治疗 计划的重要性,为 HPV 监测、预防和控制的公共卫生策略提供信息。它们还有助于理解如何使用数学模型来预测和管理 HPV 相关疾病。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the transmission dynamics of human papillomavirus (HPV) leading to cervical cancer under the combined effects of vaccination and treatment interventions. analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A deterministic mathematical model, the HPV-CCT-CM, was developed and analyzed to study the transmission dynamics of HPV and cervical cancer progression. The model incorporates compartments for susceptible, vaccinated, infected, precancerous, cancerous, treated, and recovered females, as well as susceptible, infected, and recovered males.
analysis_en.methods: The model was analyzed to establish the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium states and to examine their stability properties. The basic reproduction number, R0, and the associated stability conditions were also analyzed.
analysis_en.main_results: The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for R0 < 1. Numerical results demonstrate that the endemic equilibrium remains stable even when the effective contact rate is above 0.7 and becomes unstable when the contact rate exceeds 1.0.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that controlling HPV transmission and cervical cancer requires reducing contact rates while enhancing vaccination coverage, vaccine efficacy, and access to treatment. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for HPV surveillance, prevention, and control by highlighting the importance of reducing contact rates and improving vaccination and treatment programs. analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a deterministic mathematical model and does not account for real-world variability or data from clinical trials. title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 传播 和 宫颈癌 级数与 疫苗接种 和 治疗 的数学建模和稳定性分析
source_body_en: In this study, we develop and analyze a deterministic mathematical model, the Human Papillomavirus–Cervical Cancer Transmission and Control Model (HPV-CCT-CM), to investigate the transmission dynamics of HPV leading to cervical cancer under the combined effects of vaccination and treatment interventions. The model extends existing frameworks by incorporating compartments for susceptible, vaccinated, infected, precancerous, cancerous, treated, and recovered females, as well as susceptible, infected, and recovered males, with clinical interventions explicitly represented. We establish the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium states and analyze their stability properties. The basic reproduction number, R0, and the associated stability conditions are examined. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for R0 1. Numerical results demonstrate that the endemic equilibrium remains stable even when the effective contact rate is above 0.7 and becomes unstable when the contact rate exceeds 1.0. These findings indicate that controlling HPV transmission and cervical cancer requires reducing contact rates while enhancing vaccination coverage, vaccine efficacy, and access to treatment.

title: Brief communication: hepatitis B, human papillomavirus, pneumococcal and influenza vaccination in an Australian metropolitan HIV service
abstract: People living with HIV experience a disproportionate burden of vaccine-preventable infections. This retrospective audit assessed the proportion of patients with adequate vaccination against hepatitis B, human papillomavirus, pneumococcus and influenza within an Australian HIV service. There was a significantly higher proportion ( p < 0.001) with adequate hepatitis B vaccination (47.9%), compared to pneumococcal conjugate (19.0%), pneumococcal polysaccharide (6.6%), and human papillomavirus (7.4%) vaccination. Influenza vaccination rates (30.6%) were similar to general population rates in Western Australia. Adequate vaccination requires review to prevent hepatitis B acquisition and HPV-associated neoplasia, particularly in the context of tenofovir-free antiretroviral regimens and routine anal cancer screening.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是在澳大利亚艾滋病毒服务机构内进行的回顾性审计。它评估了具有足够的 疫苗接种 抗乙型肝炎、人乳头瘤病毒、肺炎球菌和流感的患者比例。研究设计涉及分析 疫苗接种 状态的现有记录,但没有明确报告荟萃分析或共识过程。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,与肺炎球菌结合物(19.0%)、肺炎球菌多糖(6.6%)和人乳头瘤病毒(7.4%)疫苗接种(7.4%)相比,乙型肝炎疫苗接种(47.9%)充足的患者比例明显更高。这些发现凸显了 HIV 人群中这些疾病的 疫苗接种 覆盖率差异。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,流感 疫苗接种 发病率 (30.6%) 与西澳大利亚一般人群发病率相似,这可能表明该地区没有显着差异。然而,证据并未说明 HPV 疫苗接种 感染率低的原因或 疫苗接种 在预防 HPV 相关疾病方面的有效性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该研究表明,需要对针对 HPV 的足够 疫苗接种 进行审查,以预防 HPV 相关肿瘤,特别是在不含替诺福韦的抗逆转录病毒治疗方案和常规肛门癌筛查的背景下。这表明需要针对 HIV 阳性个体进行针对性干预并改进 HPV 监测 中的 监测。

title: Coincident Detection of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) in the Oral and Genital Regions in a Young Adult Male with Oral Lichen Planus: A Case Report
abstract: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is an atypical presentation in young males, and its co-occurrence with human papillomavirus (HPV) raises clinical concerns regarding malignant transformation. This case report describes a 27-year-old sexually active male with OLP and potentially persistent, synchronous oral and multigenotypic genital HPV co-infections. A 27-year-old male presented for follow-up 19 months after surgical excision of an oral papilloma with lichenoid features and histopathologically confirmed OLP. Molecular detection and genotyping were performed using oral and genital swabs via CFX96 real-time PCR. Results revealed potentially persistent oral co-infection with high-risk HPV 31 and low-risk HPV 44. Genital screening detected these same oral genotypes alongside four additional strains, consisting of high-risk HPV 18, 35, and 73 (classified per IARC standards), and low-risk HPV 81, with clinically evident condylomata acuminata. The long-term detection of high-risk HPV 31 in the oral swab in the presence of OLP highlights a hypothetical “dual-hit” oncogenic framework, where inflammation-induced oxidative stress may synergize with viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins to disrupt cell cycle regulation and elevate malignant transformation risks, though this remains entirely speculative in the absence of mechanistic biomarkers. Synchronous oral and anogenital HPV co-infections in young patients with OLP warrant a comprehensive multidisciplinary diagnostic protocol and cautious oncologic surveillance recommendations to prevent malignant progression and further transmission.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the co-occurrence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in the oral and genital regions in a young adult male with oral lichen planus (OLP), addressing the clinical concern of potential malignant transformation.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This case report described a 27-year-old sexually active male with OLP and potentially persistent, synchronous oral and multigenotypic genital HPV co-infections.
elements_en.methods: Molecular detection and genotyping were performed using oral and genital swabs via CFX96 real-time PCR.
elements_en.main_results: Results revealed potentially persistent oral co-infection with high-risk HPV 31 and low-risk HPV 44, alongside four additional strains in the genital region, including high-risk HPV 18, 35, and 73, and low-risk HPV 81.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The long-term detection of high-risk HPV 31 in the oral swab in the presence of OLP highlights a hypothetical “dual-hit” oncogenic framework, where inflammation-induced oxidative stress may synergize with viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins to disrupt cell cycle regulation and elevate malignant transformation risks, though this remains entirely speculative in the absence of mechanistic biomarkers.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Synchronous oral and anogenital HPV co-infections in young patients with OLP warrant a comprehensive multidisciplinary diagnostic protocol and cautious oncologic surveillance recommendations to prevent malignant progression and further transmission.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its case report design, which does not allow for generalization of findings.

title_zh: 在患有口腔扁平苔藓的年轻成年男性的口腔和生殖器区域同时检测到 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV):病例报告
source_body_en: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is an atypical presentation in young males, and its co-occurrence with human papillomavirus (HPV) raises clinical concerns regarding malignant transformation. This case report describes a 27-year-old sexually active male with OLP and potentially persistent, synchronous oral and multigenotypic genital HPV co-infections. A 27-year-old male presented for follow-up 19 months after surgical excision of an oral papilloma with lichenoid features and histopathologically confirmed OLP. Molecular detection and genotyping were performed using oral and genital swabs via CFX96 real-time PCR. Results revealed potentially persistent oral co-infection with high-risk HPV 31 and low-risk HPV 44. Genital screening detected these same oral genotypes alongside four additional strains, consisting of high-risk HPV 18, 35, and 73 (classified per IARC standards), and low-risk HPV 81, with clinically evident condylomata acuminata. The long-term detection of high-risk HPV 31 in the oral swab in the presence of OLP highlights a hypothetical “dual-hit” oncogenic framework, where inflammation-induced oxidative stress may synergize with viral E6 and E7 oncoproteins to disrupt cell cycle regulation and elevate malignant transformation risks, though this remains entirely speculative in the absence of mechanistic biomarkers. Synchronous oral and anogenital HPV co-infections in young patients with OLP warrant a comprehensive multidisciplinary diagnostic protocol and cautious oncologic surveillance recommendations to prevent malignant progression and further transmission.
abstract_zh: 口腔扁平苔藓 (OLP) 是年轻男性的一种非典型表现,其与 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 的共存引起了临床对恶性转化的担忧。病例报告 描述了一名性活跃的 27 岁男性,患有 OLP,并可能持续、同步口腔和多基因型生殖器 HPV 合并感染。一名 27 岁男性在手术切除具有苔藓样特征且经组织病理学证实的 OLP 的口腔乳头状瘤后 19 个月进行随访。通过 CFX96 实时 PCR 使用口腔和生殖器拭子进行分子检测和基因分型。结果显示,高危型HPV 31 和低风险 HPV 44 可能存在持续性口腔双重感染。生殖器筛查检测到这些相同的口腔基因型以及另外四种菌株,包括 高危型HPV 18、35 和 73(根据 IARC 标准分类)和低风险 HPV 81,具有临床明显的尖锐湿疣。在 OLP 存在的情况下,在口腔拭子中长期检测到 高危型HPV 31 突显了一种假设的“双重打击”致癌框架,其中炎症诱导的氧化应激可能与病毒 E6 和 E7 癌蛋白协同作用,破坏细胞周期调节并提高恶性转化风险,尽管在缺乏机械生物标志物的情况下,这仍然完全是推测性的。年轻 OLP 患者同时口腔和肛门生殖器 HPV 合并感染需要综合的多学科诊断方案和谨慎的肿瘤学 监测 建议,以防止恶性进展和进一步 传播。

title: Human Papillomavirus-Associated Cancers and the Potential Role of Local Bacterial Populations
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infectious agent in the United States as well as globally. This review aims to examine neoplastic diseases associated with HPV with special emphasis on cancers of the uterine cervix and oropharynx. Among the group of high-risk HPVs, i.e., types of HPV that can cause abnormal cellular changes leading to malignancies, HPV genotypes 16 and 18 are commonly found in cervical cancer, whereas HPV-16 is the most detected HPV in oropharyngeal cancer. It is known that the HPV genome comprises three major functional regions: the early region, which encodes proteins such as E6 and E7; the long control region; and the late region, which encodes structural capsid proteins L1 and L2. The E6 and E7 proteins are pivotal to carcinogenesis. E6 promotes degradation of the tumor suppressor p53, while E7 inactivates the retinoblastoma protein, critically disrupting cell cycle regulation and enabling uncontrolled proliferation. These disruptions promote survival of HPV-infected cells–a requirement for the viral life cycle. The viral L1, the major capsid component, is used for classification, PCR detection, antigenic tests, and in prophylactic vaccine preparation. However, it is important to correlate the role of HPV with different risk factors, particularly when considering a wide variation in cervical cancer incidence rates in different nations and geographic regions. Compared to cervical cancer, HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer risk factors are thought to be associated with sexual behavior primarily. Overall, the local microbial environment of both the cervicovaginal region and the oral cavity may play a significant role in cancer development. For example, an increase in certain bacteria has been documented in the course of disease, such as Fusobacterium in oropharyngeal cancer or Prevotella and Gardnerella in bacterial vaginosis. On the other hand, a depletion of beneficial bacteria in the cervicovaginal environment may contribute to the development of cervical neoplasia. In the case of cervical cancer, all risk factors possibly alter the cervicovaginal microbial flora adversely. The dominance of anaerobic bacteria could bring about pathological changes. In relation to the disease progression, an increasing level of Lactobacillus depletion has been reported. Similarly, in different head and neck cancers, investigators documented differences in bacterial genera between HPV-positive and HPV-negative cases. Furthermore, some investigators suggested that certain bacteria could serve as cancer biomarkers in oral regions. Various bacteria are present throughout the gastrointestinal tract, particularly in the large intestine (colon), where they form the largest populations, and they influence diverse pathophysiological processes both inside and outside the gut. The gut microbiota is a typical example of how alterations in it could be associated with pathological processes, including cancer development. Regarding their impact on other organs, different bidirectional communication networks have been proposed. One pertinent example is the gut–vaginal axis, which connects the microbial communities of these two organs. Currently, a growing number of studies are trying to manipulate this axis and reconstitute the cervicovaginal microbial flora in a favorable manner. Therefore, appropriate modifications of the local microbial environment could prevent pathological processes in an economical way.

On the other hand, a depletion of beneficial bacteria in the cervicovaginal environment may contribute to the development of cervical neoplasia. In the case of cervical cancer, all risk factors possibly alter the cervicovaginal microbial flora adversely. The dominance of anaerobic bacteria could bring about pathological changes. In relation to the disease progression, an increasing level of Lactobacillus depletion has been reported. Various bacteria are present throughout the gastrointestinal tract, particularly in the large intestine (colon), where they form the largest populations, and they influence diverse pathophysiological processes both inside and outside the gut. The gut microbiota is a typical example of how alterations in it could be associated with pathological processes, including cancer development. Regarding their impact on other organs, different bidirectional communication networks have been proposed. One pertinent example is the gut–vaginal axis, which connects the microbial communities of these two organs. Currently, a growing number of studies are trying to manipulate this axis and reconstitute the cervicovaginal microbial flora in a favorable manner. Therefore, appropriate modifications of the local microbial environment could prevent pathological processes in an economical way.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of human papillomaviruses (HPVs) in neoplastic diseases, particularly cervical and oropharyngeal cancers. It highlights the significance of high-risk HPV genotypes, such as HPV-16 and HPV-18, in these conditions. The review discusses the functional regions of the HPV genome and the pivotal role of E6 and E7 proteins in carcinogenesis. It also emphasizes the importance of the local microbial environment in cancer development, noting that alterations in bacterial populations may contribute to disease progression. The review suggests that modifying the microbial flora could be an effective strategy for prevention. However, it acknowledges the need for further research to understand the complex interactions between HPV and the microbiome, as well as the variations in cancer incidence across different populations.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 是美国乃至全球最常见的性传播传染病。本综述旨在检查与 HPV 相关的肿瘤疾病,特别关注宫颈癌和口咽癌。在 高危型HPV 组(即可引起异常细胞变化并导致恶性肿瘤的 HPV 类型)中,HPV 基因型 16 和 18 在 宫颈癌 中常见,而 HPV-16 是口咽癌中检测最多的 HPV。据了解,HPV 基因组包含三个主要功能区:早期区,编码E6、E7等蛋白;长控制区;和晚期区域,编码结构衣壳蛋白 L1 和 L2。E6 和 E7 蛋白对于致癌作用至关重要。E6 促进肿瘤抑制因子 p53 的降解,而 E7 则使视网膜母细胞瘤蛋白失活,严重破坏细胞周期调节并导致增殖不受控制。这些破坏促进了 HPV 感染细胞的存活——这是病毒生命周期的要求。病毒 L1 是主要衣壳成分,用于分类、PCR 检测、抗原测试和预防性 疫苗 制备。然而,将 HPV 的作用与不同的危险因素联系起来非常重要,特别是考虑到不同国家和地理区域的 宫颈癌 发病率 比率存在很大差异时。与宫颈癌相比,HPV阳性口咽癌危险因素被认为主要与性行为有关。总体而言,宫颈阴道区域和口腔的局部微生物环境可能在癌症的发展中发挥重要作用。例如,某些细菌在疾病过程中有所增加,例如口咽癌中的梭杆菌或细菌性阴道病中的普雷沃氏菌和加德纳氏菌。另一方面,宫颈阴道环境中有益细菌的消耗可能会导致宫颈肿瘤的发生。就 宫颈癌 而言,所有危险因素都可能对宫颈阴道微生物菌群产生不利改变。厌氧菌占优势,可引起病理变化。据报道,与疾病进展相关的是,乳酸菌消耗水平不断增加。同样,在不同的头颈癌中,研究人员记录了 HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性病例之间细菌属的差异。此外,一些研究人员认为某些细菌可以作为口腔区域的癌症生物标志物。各种细菌存在于整个胃肠道中,特别是在大肠(结肠)中,它们在那里形成最大的种群,并且影响肠道内外的多种病理生理过程。肠道微生物群是其变化如何与包括癌症发展在内的病理过程相关的典型例子。关于它们对其他器官的影响,已经提出了不同的双向通信网络。一个相关的例子是肠道-阴道轴,它连接这两个器官的微生物群落。目前,越来越多的研究正在尝试操纵该轴并以有利的方式重建宫颈阴道微生物菌群。因此,适当改变局部微生物环境可以以经济的方式预防病理过程。

title: Systemic inflammatory markers do not independently predict positive surgical margins after loop electrosurgical excision procedure in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Objective : To investigate the predictive value of preoperative clinicopathological factors and systemic inflammatory markers for positive surgical margin after loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3), and to develop a nomogram prediction model. Methods : A total of 1,373 patients with CIN3 who underwent LEEP at Hubei Provincial Maternal and Child Health Hospital between January 2021 and December 2025 were retrospectively included. Patients were randomly assigned at a 7:3 ratio to a training set "n=961" and a validation set "n=412" . Preoperative demographic characteristics, cytology results (TCT grade), HPV genotypes, colposcopic biopsy pathology, and hematological parameters (including complete blood count, coagulation, and lipid profiles) were collected. LASSO regression was used to select predictors in the training set, followed by multivariable logistic regression analysis. Model discrimination was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration by calibration plots and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis (DCA). A nomogram was constructed based on the final model. Results : A total of 1,373 CIN3 patients were included, among whom 129 (9.4%) had positive surgical margins. LASSO regression identified five predictors: TCT grade, age, BMI, multiple HPV infection, and parity. Multivariable logistic regression showed that TCT grade (aOR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.10–1.48, P = 0.002) and age "aOR=1.05,P Conclusion : A nomogram based on preoperative TCT grade, age, BMI, multiple HPV infection, and parity can accurately predict the risk of positive margin after LEEP in CIN3 patients, with a validation AUC of 0.80. Systemic inflammatory markers do not independently predict margin status. This model may assist in preoperative risk assessment and individualized surgical decision-making.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨术前临床病理因素和全身炎症标志物对宫颈上皮内瘤变3级(CIN3)患者宫颈环形电切术(LEEP)术后切缘阳性的预测价值,并建立列线图预测模型。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 湖北省妇幼保健院开展了一项单中心回顾性研究,纳入 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间接受 LEEP 的 1,373 例 CIN3 患者。患者按 7:3 的比例随机分配到训练组(n=961)和验证组(n=412)。
elements_zh.methods: 收集术前人口统计学特征、细胞学结果(TCT分级)、HPV基因型、阴道镜活检病理学和血液学参数。使用 LASSO 回归在训练集中选择预测变量,然后进行多变量逻辑回归分析。模型辨别力通过受试者工作特征曲线 (AUC) 下面积、校准图和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验进行校准以及决策曲线分析 (DCA) 的临床效用进行评估。根据最终模型构建列线图。
elements_zh.main_results: 总共纳入 1,373 例 CIN3 患者,其中 129 例(9.4%)手术切缘呈阳性。全身炎症标志物不能独立预测切缘状态。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,基于术前 TCT 分级、年龄、BMI、多重 HPV 感染和产次的列线图可以准确预测 CIN3 患者 LEEP 后切缘阳性的风险,验证 AUC 为 0.80。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该模型可能有助于CIN3患者的术前风险评估和个体化手术决策。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项单中心回顾性研究,可能限制普遍性。证据仅基于抽象数据,研究结果的可信度中等。

title_zh: 全身炎症标志物不能独立预测 3 级宫颈上皮内瘤变患者行环形电切术后切缘阳性:一项单中心回顾性研究
source_body_en: Abstract Objective : To investigate the predictive value of preoperative clinicopathological factors and systemic inflammatory markers for positive surgical margin after loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3), and to develop a nomogram prediction model. Methods : A total of 1,373 patients with CIN3 who underwent LEEP at Hubei Provincial Maternal and Child Health Hospital between January 2021 and December 2025 were retrospectively included. Patients were randomly assigned at a 7:3 ratio to a training set "n=961" and a validation set "n=412" . Preoperative demographic characteristics, cytology results (TCT grade), HPV genotypes, colposcopic biopsy pathology, and hematological parameters (including complete blood count, coagulation, and lipid profiles) were collected. LASSO regression was used to select predictors in the training set, followed by multivariable logistic regression analysis. Model discrimination was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration by calibration plots and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis (DCA). A nomogram was constructed based on the final model. Results : A total of 1,373 CIN3 patients were included, among whom 129 (9.4%) had positive surgical margins. LASSO regression identified five predictors: TCT grade, age, BMI, multiple HPV infection, and parity. Multivariable logistic regression showed that TCT grade (aOR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.10–1.48, P = 0.002) and age "aOR=1.05,P Conclusion : A nomogram based on preoperative TCT grade, age, BMI, multiple HPV infection, and parity can accurately predict the risk of positive margin after LEEP in CIN3 patients, with a validation AUC of 0.80. Systemic inflammatory markers do not independently predict margin status. This model may assist in preoperative risk assessment and individualized surgical decision-making.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨术前临床病理因素和全身炎症标志物对宫颈上皮内瘤变3级(CIN3)患者宫颈环形电切术(LEEP)术后切缘阳性的预测价值,并建立列线图预测模型。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 湖北省妇幼保健院开展了一项单中心回顾性研究,纳入 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间接受 LEEP 的 1,373 例 CIN3 患者。患者按 7:3 的比例随机分配到训练组(n=961)和验证组(n=412)。
analysis_zh.methods: 收集术前人口统计学特征、细胞学结果(TCT分级)、HPV基因型、阴道镜活检病理学和血液学参数。使用 LASSO 回归在训练集中选择预测变量,然后进行多变量逻辑回归分析。模型辨别力通过受试者工作特征曲线 (AUC) 下面积、校准图和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验进行校准以及决策曲线分析 (DCA) 的临床效用进行评估。根据最终模型构建列线图。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总共纳入 1,373 例 CIN3 患者,其中 129 例(9.4%)手术切缘呈阳性。全身炎症标志物不能独立预测切缘状态。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,基于术前 TCT 分级、年龄、BMI、多重 HPV 感染和产次的列线图可以准确预测 CIN3 患者 LEEP 后切缘阳性的风险,验证 AUC 为 0.80。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该模型可能有助于CIN3患者的术前风险评估和个体化手术决策。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项单中心回顾性研究,可能限制普遍性。证据仅基于抽象数据,研究结果的可信度中等。

title: Divergent Human Papillomavirus Genotype Spectra in Three Indigenous Communities of Venezuela: Implications for Vaccine Choice and Cervical Screening
abstract: Background: Genotype-resolved data on human papillomavirus (HPV) are almost absent for Venezuelan indigenous women. Methods: We studied 260 women from La Guajira (Wayuu, n = 94), Maniapure (Eñepa, n = 141), and Delta Amacuro (Warao, n = 25), processing all self-collected samples with a single real-time PCR assay that resolves 21 genotypes; cytology was available for 144. Results: HPV prevalence was 55.4% (95% CI 49.3–61.3) and high-risk prevalence was 51.2% (95% CI 45.1–57.2), rising from 42.6% in La Guajira to 59.6% in Maniapure and 80.0% in Delta Amacuro (p = 0.001). Nineteen genotypes were detected. HPV-31 was most frequent (15.8%), followed by HPV-16 (11.5%), and each community had its own profile, with HPV-68 and HPV-56 leading in Delta Amacuro. Half of the infected women carried more than one type. Cytology and HPV testing overlapped little: 20 of 78 HPV-positive women with a smear (25.6%) had an abnormal result (κ = 0.056). At least one nonavalent vaccine type was present in 69.4% of infected women, compared with 30.6% for the bivalent vaccine. Conclusions: HPV vaccination is not part of the Venezuelan national program; these data favor the nonavalent formulation, and HPV-based screening would need a feasible triage pathway for the many women who test positive.

title_zh: 委内瑞拉三个土著社区中人乳头瘤病毒基因型谱的差异:对疫苗选择和宫颈筛查的启示
source_body_en: Background: Genotype-resolved data on human papillomavirus (HPV) are almost absent for Venezuelan indigenous women. Methods: We studied 260 women from La Guajira (Wayuu, n = 94), Maniapure (Eñepa, n = 141), and Delta Amacuro (Warao, n = 25), processing all self-collected samples with a single real-time PCR assay that resolves 21 genotypes; cytology was available for 144. Results: HPV prevalence was 55.4% (95% CI 49.3–61.3) and high-risk prevalence was 51.2% (95% CI 45.1–57.2), rising from 42.6% in La Guajira to 59.6% in Maniapure and 80.0% in Delta Amacuro (p = 0.001). Nineteen genotypes were detected. HPV-31 was most frequent (15.8%), followed by HPV-16 (11.5%), and each community had its own profile, with HPV-68 and HPV-56 leading in Delta Amacuro. Half of the infected women carried more than one type. Cytology and HPV testing overlapped little: 20 of 78 HPV-positive women with a smear (25.6%) had an abnormal result (κ = 0.056). At least one nonavalent vaccine type was present in 69.4% of infected women, compared with 30.6% for the bivalent vaccine. Conclusions: HPV vaccination is not part of the Venezuelan national program; these data favor the nonavalent formulation, and HPV-based screening would need a feasible triage pathway for the many women who test positive.

title: Health beliefs and parental responses to human papillomavirus vaccination in the Middle East: a theory-informed narrative synthesis guided by the health belief model
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection in women and the primary cause of cervical cancer (CC). HPV vaccination and screening programs have significantly reduced CC incidence and mortality worldwide, preventing up to 70% of HPV-related CC and 90% of genital warts. Developing effective vaccination strategies is therefore essential. Objectives This study systematically synthesizes the attitudes and health beliefs of Middle Eastern (ME) parents regarding HPV vaccination, examines parental vaccine uptake, and assesses uptake among their children. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between January 2006 and May 2025. Thirty-three studies were included. A theory-informed narrative synthesis of predominantly quantitative evidence was conducted, with deductive mapping of findings to the health belief model (HBM) constructs. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025645551). Results The review included 32 quantitative cross-sectional studies and one qualitative study, involving 18,170 participants. Findings were organized according to HBM constructs, including perceived susceptibility, severity, barriers, benefits, self-efficacy, and cues to action. Parents generally demonstrated limited knowledge of HPV and vaccination. Major barriers included safety concerns, cost, limited access, lack of healthcare provider recommendations, and insufficient information. Cultural and systemic factors were also associated with vaccine uptake. Conclusion HPV-related knowledge in ME countries remains insufficient and is frequently associated with vaccination attitudes and acceptance across the included studies. Improving uptake requires targeted educational interventions, healthcare provider engagement, public health campaigns, financial support, and policy-level initiatives. Strengthening awareness and addressing structural barriers are critical for enhancing vaccination acceptance. Self-efficacy, where directly reported, appeared to be associated with more favorable vaccine attitudes; however, direct evidence for parental self-efficacy as a distinct HBM construct was limited across the included studies and should not be overstated. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/myprospero/CRD42025645551 .

Objectives This study systematically synthesizes the attitudes and health beliefs of Middle Eastern (ME) parents regarding HPV vaccination, examines parental vaccine uptake, and assesses uptake among their children. A theory-informed narrative synthesis of predominantly quantitative evidence was conducted, with deductive mapping of findings to the health belief model (HBM) constructs. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025645551). Results The review included 32 quantitative cross-sectional studies and one qualitative study, involving 18,170 participants. Findings were organized according to HBM constructs, including perceived susceptibility, severity, barriers, benefits, self-efficacy, and cues to action. Parents generally demonstrated limited knowledge of HPV and vaccination. Major barriers included safety concerns, cost, limited access, lack of healthcare provider recommendations, and insufficient information. Cultural and systemic factors were also associated with vaccine uptake. Conclusion HPV-related knowledge in ME countries remains insufficient and is frequently associated with vaccination attitudes and acceptance across the included studies. Improving uptake requires targeted educational interventions, healthcare provider engagement, public health campaigns, financial support, and policy-level initiatives. Strengthening awareness and addressing structural barriers are critical for enhancing vaccination acceptance. title: Serum Free Fatty Acid-Based Diagnostic Index for Cervical Cancer Including High-Risk HPV-Negative Cases: An Independent Validation Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer (CC) is usually caused by high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV); however, some hrHPV-negative cases are undetectable by current screening programs. We evaluated a previously established diagnostic model based on serum free fatty acids (FFAs) in an independent cohort including hrHPV-negative CC. Methods: We analyzed serum FFAs from 101 patients with CC (16 hrHPV-negative), 60 healthy donors, and 16 patients with benign gynecological diseases, none of whom were included in the previous study, and gene expression levels of fatty acid metabolism-related enzymes in 64 surgical CC and five normal cervix samples. Results: Levels of nine FFAs differed between CC and the non-cancer groups but not between hrHPV-negative and hrHPV-positive CC. Gene expression levels of acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1, fatty acid synthase, stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1, and monoacylglycerol lipase were increased in CC compared with normal tissues, with no significant differences between hrHPV-negative and hrHPV-positive CC. The previous model (diagnostic index = −5.631 + 0.030 × (stearic acid) + 9.188 × (dihomo-γ-linolenic acid)) distinguished CC from the non-cancer groups (area under the curve, 0.969). At the pre-specified cut-off value, sensitivity was 97.0% (hrHPV-negative CC, 93.8%) and specificity in healthy donors was 58.3%; at the cut-off value derived in this cohort, these were 82.2% (93.8%) and 98.3%, respectively. In hrHPV-negative CC, the positivity rate exceeded those of squamous cell carcinoma antigen, carcinoembryonic antigen, and CA125. Conclusions: The serum-FFA-based diagnostic model detected CC, including hrHPV-negative cases, in an independent cohort. With calibration of the cut-off value, this approach may complement existing HPV-based testing.

title: Shifting High-Risk HPV Genotype Patterns in Histologically Confirmed Cervical HSIL: Temporal Changes and Differential Distribution in Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes differ in their oncogenic potential and contribution to cervical precancer and invasive cancer. We investigated temporal changes in HR-HPV genotype patterns in histologically confirmed cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and differences between 2022–2025 HSIL and invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in an opportunistic screening setting in Spain. This retrospective study included 371 patients with HSIL from 2011 to 2016, 411 with HSIL from 2022 to 2025, and 65 with SCC from 2022 to 2025. Among HR-HPV-positive HSIL, HPV16/18 frequency decreased from 65.7% to 50.8% (p = 0.003), accompanied by a lower mean number of detected genotypes. After adjustment for age and cytological diagnosis, the 2022–2025 period was associated with lower odds of HPV16 (OR 0.59) and HPV18 (OR 0.36) detection. Compared with 2022–2025 HSIL, SCC showed higher HPV16/18 frequency (75.0% vs. 50.8%; p = 0.003), fewer multiple infections, and lower representation of other HR-HPV genotypes. Exploratory birth-cohort analysis showed lower HPV16/18 frequency in women born in or after 1994, with higher individual frequencies of HPV52 and HPV58. HR-HPV genotype patterns in histologically confirmed HSIL varied over time and between birth cohorts, while invasive SCC showed greater HPV16/18 representation and lower HPV diversity.

title: High-Risk HPV Positivity With NILM Cytology: The Added Value of HPV Genotyping in a Case Report
abstract: Background: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity with negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM) cytology represents a discordant cervical cancer screening result in which HPV DNA is detected despite the absence of cytological evidence of an intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. HPV genotyping and molecular triage approaches have been evaluated to further characterise risk among HPV-positive women. Case Presentation: A cervical cytology specimen obtained during cervical cancer screening was processed using liquid-based cytology with the ThinPrep® system and Papanicolaou staining. Microscopic examination demonstrated a satisfactory specimen with adequate representation of squamous epithelial cells and no cytological evidence of intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV testing was performed using polymerase chain reaction with the Xpert® HPV HR assay on the GeneXpert® Dx System. HPV16 and HPV18/45 were negative, as were the HPV31/35/33/52/58 and HPV51/59 genotype groups. HPV DNA was detected within the HPV39/68/56/66 genotype group. Sample adequacy and probe check controls passed, and the test was completed successfully without an error. Integrated Interpretation: The case demonstrates an HR-HPV-positive/NILM cytological pattern. The positive molecular result indicates detection of high-risk HPV DNA but does not establish the presence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or a precancerous lesion. Because the Xpert® HPV HR assay reports the positive result as a genotype group, the specific genotype responsible for the positive result cannot be determined from this test alone. Conclusion: This case illustrates the added information provided by HPV genotype-group analysis in an HR-HPV-positive/NILM screening result. The findings support risk-based clinical follow-up according to applicable cervical cancer screening guidelines rather than a diagnosis of precancerous disease.

title_zh: 高危型HPV NILM 细胞学检测的阳性结果:病例报告 中 HPV 基因分型的附加价值
source_body_en: Background: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity with negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM) cytology represents a discordant cervical cancer screening result in which HPV DNA is detected despite the absence of cytological evidence of an intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. HPV genotyping and molecular triage approaches have been evaluated to further characterise risk among HPV-positive women. Case Presentation: A cervical cytology specimen obtained during cervical cancer screening was processed using liquid-based cytology with the ThinPrep® system and Papanicolaou staining. Microscopic examination demonstrated a satisfactory specimen with adequate representation of squamous epithelial cells and no cytological evidence of intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV testing was performed using polymerase chain reaction with the Xpert® HPV HR assay on the GeneXpert® Dx System. HPV16 and HPV18/45 were negative, as were the HPV31/35/33/52/58 and HPV51/59 genotype groups. HPV DNA was detected within the HPV39/68/56/66 genotype group. Sample adequacy and probe check controls passed, and the test was completed successfully without an error. Integrated Interpretation: The case demonstrates an HR-HPV-positive/NILM cytological pattern. The positive molecular result indicates detection of high-risk HPV DNA but does not establish the presence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or a precancerous lesion. Because the Xpert® HPV HR assay reports the positive result as a genotype group, the specific genotype responsible for the positive result cannot be determined from this test alone. Conclusion: This case illustrates the added information provided by HPV genotype-group analysis in an HR-HPV-positive/NILM screening result. The findings support risk-based clinical follow-up according to applicable cervical cancer screening guidelines rather than a diagnosis of precancerous disease.
abstract_zh: 背景:高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 阳性且上皮内病变或恶性肿瘤 (NILM) 细胞学阴性代表不一致的 宫颈癌 筛查结果,其中尽管没有上皮内病变或恶性肿瘤的细胞学证据,但仍检测到 HPV DNA。已经对 HPV 基因分型和分子分类方法进行了评估,以进一步描述 HPV 阳性女性的风险特征。病例介绍:在 宫颈癌 筛查期间获得的宫颈细胞学标本使用 ThinPrep® 系统和巴氏染色的液基细胞学进行处理。显微镜检查显示标本令人满意,具有足够的鳞状上皮细胞代表性,并且没有上皮内病变或恶性肿瘤的细胞学证据。高危型HPV 测试是在 GeneXpert® Dx 系统上使用聚合酶链反应和 Xpert® HPV HR 测定进行的。HPV16 和 HPV18/45 以及 HPV31/35/33/52/58 和 HPV51/59 基因型组均为阴性。在 HPV39/68/56/66 基因型组中检测到 HPV DNA。样品充足性和探针检查控制已通过,测试成功完成,没有出现错误。综合解读:该病例表现出 HR-HPV 阳性/NILM 细胞学模式。阳性分子结果表明检测到 高危型HPV DNA,但并不能确定宫颈上皮内瘤变或癌前病变的存在。由于 Xpert® HPV HR 检测将阳性结果报告为基因型组,因此无法仅通过该检测确定导致阳性结果的特定基因型。结论:本病例说明了 HR-HPV 阳性/NILM 筛查结果中 HPV 基因型组分析提供的附加信息。研究结果支持根据适用的 宫颈癌 筛查指南而不是癌前疾病的 诊断 进行基于风险的临床随访。

title: Excisional biopsy of neck lymph node in HPV positive oropharyngeal cancer associated with human papillomavirus
abstract: The course of HPV positive oropharyngeal cancer is often characterized by minimal symptoms caused by small primary tumor coupled with clinically apparent neck metastases. In those cases, the diagnosis of oropharyngeal cancer is frequently made post factum after initial excisional biopsy of neck lymph node. The aim of the study was to analyze the rate and the prognostic influence of that diagnostics variant. METHODS AND MATERIALS. Patients with HPV positive T1-2 oropharyngeal cancer with clinically apparent neck metastases were included into the study. The diagnosis was made in a standard manner before treatment in patients of Group 1. Patients of Group 2 previously underwent excisional biopsy of neck lymph node and only then referred to specialized clinic. Oncologic treatment results were assessed with the rate of local, regional recurrence and Kaplan – Meyer overall survival. After applying the inclusion criteria, 53 patients aged between 34 and 74 years were identified with 34 and 19 of them in Group 1 and 2. In both Groups, tonsil lesions (68 % and 89 %) and T2 tumors (76 % and 58 %) were more prevalent. Neck lump was the only symptom in 50 % and 68 % of cases. Transoral approach was used most often (62 % and 63 %). Neck dissection was performed in all patients. Adjuvant radiation was employed in 82 % and 63 % of cases. The rate of local, regional recurrence, locoregional control and Kaplan–Meyer overall survival for all subjects were 3.8 %, 5.7 %, 92.4 % and 87 % without statistical significance between the Group 1 and 2. Hypodiagnostics of oropharyngeal cancer is a widespread phenomenon and, to a great extent, can be explained by subjective reasons. Increasing awareness of the disease course by ambulatory physicians and general surgeons may raise the chance of establishing the prompt correct diagnosis. Deviation of basic oncologic principles of therapy is not accompanied by impairment of results.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study included 53 patients with HPV positive T1-2 oropharyngeal cancer and clinically apparent neck metastases, divided into two groups based on the diagnostic approach.
elements_en.methods: The study analyzed the rate of local, regional recurrence and Kaplan–Meyer overall survival, using tonsil lesions, T2 tumors, and transoral approach as key parameters.
elements_en.main_results: The rate of local, regional recurrence, locoregional control, and Kaplan–Meyer overall survival were 3.8%, 5.7%, 92.4%, and 87% respectively, without statistical significance between the two groups.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that deviation from basic oncologic principles of therapy did not impair results, suggesting that the diagnostic approach did not significantly affect outcomes.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the diagnostic approach does not impact treatment outcomes, which could inform clinical practice and raise awareness among ambulatory physicians and general surgeons.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design limitations, such as the small sample size and lack of randomization, may affect the generalizability of the findings.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 相关 HPV 阳性口咽癌颈部淋巴结切除活检
source_body_en: The course of HPV positive oropharyngeal cancer is often characterized by minimal symptoms caused by small primary tumor coupled with clinically apparent neck metastases. In those cases, the diagnosis of oropharyngeal cancer is frequently made post factum after initial excisional biopsy of neck lymph node. The aim of the study was to analyze the rate and the prognostic influence of that diagnostics variant. METHODS AND MATERIALS. Patients with HPV positive T1-2 oropharyngeal cancer with clinically apparent neck metastases were included into the study. The diagnosis was made in a standard manner before treatment in patients of Group 1. Patients of Group 2 previously underwent excisional biopsy of neck lymph node and only then referred to specialized clinic. Oncologic treatment results were assessed with the rate of local, regional recurrence and Kaplan – Meyer overall survival. After applying the inclusion criteria, 53 patients aged between 34 and 74 years were identified with 34 and 19 of them in Group 1 and 2. In both Groups, tonsil lesions (68 % and 89 %) and T2 tumors (76 % and 58 %) were more prevalent. Neck lump was the only symptom in 50 % and 68 % of cases. Transoral approach was used most often (62 % and 63 %). Neck dissection was performed in all patients. Adjuvant radiation was employed in 82 % and 63 % of cases. The rate of local, regional recurrence, locoregional control and Kaplan–Meyer overall survival for all subjects were 3.8 %, 5.7 %, 92.4 % and 87 % without statistical significance between the Group 1 and 2. Hypodiagnostics of oropharyngeal cancer is a widespread phenomenon and, to a great extent, can be explained by subjective reasons. Increasing awareness of the disease course by ambulatory physicians and general surgeons may raise the chance of establishing the prompt correct diagnosis. Deviation of basic oncologic principles of therapy is not accompanied by impairment of results.

title: New form of HPV18 L1 found in native virions contributes to virion stability and infectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Current dogma states that papillomavirus virions consist of only one form of the L1 major capsid protein. Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) have been studied using recombinant particles, thereby bypassing the need to grow the virus in a model of differentiating epithelium. Expression vectors engineered to produce L1 utilize a consensus methionine found in many HPV types. However, HPV18 has two additional in-frame methionine residues located 61 and 26 amino acids upstream of the consensus methionine. These methionine residues are excluded from the L1 expression vector used to create the recombinant virus. On the other hand, HPV produced from organotypic raft culture allows virions to be assembled in a differentiating epithelium in the presence of its native promoters and complete genome. Here, we have utilized this system to show that the wild-type HPV18, produced in a more natural setting, translates a larger form of L1 from the upstream methionine, which is 61 amino acid residues upstream from the consensus methionine, and a smaller form from the consensus methionine, with both sizes assembled in the newly formed virion. Ablation of the upstream methionine residue at position 61 altered the virion capsid conformation, and also decreased virion stability and infectivity. IMPORTANCE The present study investigates whether the papillomavirus virions contain more than one isoform of the L1 major capsid protein. By using organotypic raft cultures that mimic the naturally differentiating epithelium, we revealed that wild-type HPV18 expresses and incorporates two distinct L1 isoforms into the virion, including a previously unrecognized longer form translated from an upstream methionine. Our study has further shown that disruption of the upstream methionine impairs virion stability and infectivity, demonstrating that the longer L1 isoform contributes to proper capsid architecture and viral function. These findings offer a new understanding of HPV capsid biology and have significant implications for the future development of HPV vaccines, diagnostics, and antiviral therapies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用器官型筏培养物来模拟自然分化的上皮,其中使用其天然启动子和完整的 基因组 产生野生型 HPV18。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员采用器官型筏培养物产生 HPV18 病毒颗粒,并分析了两种不同 L1 亚型的表达和掺入,包括从上游甲硫氨酸翻译而来的较长形式。
elements_zh.main_results: 61位上游甲硫氨酸残基的消融改变了病毒体衣壳构象,降低了病毒体稳定性和感染性,并揭示了野生型HPV18表达两种不同的L1亚型并将其整合到病毒体中。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,较长的 L1 亚型有助于正确的衣壳结构和病毒功能,为 HPV 衣壳生物学提供了新的认识。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对 HPV 疫苗、诊断和 抗病毒药物 疗法的未来发展具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅基于抽象证据,结果来自单一 HPV 类型,这可能会限制对其他 HPV 类型的普遍适用性。

abstract_zh: 摘要 当前的教条指出,乳头瘤病毒病毒体仅由 L1 主要衣壳蛋白的一种形式组成。人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 已使用重组颗粒进行了研究,从而绕过了在分化上皮模型中培养病毒的需要。表达 媒介 被设计用于利用许多 HPV 类型中发现的共有蛋氨酸产生 L1。然而,HPV18 有两个额外的框内蛋氨酸残基,位于共有蛋氨酸上游 61 和 26 个氨基酸处。这些甲硫氨酸残基被排除在用于创建重组病毒的 L1 表达 媒介 之外。另一方面,由器官筏培养产生的 HPV 允许病毒粒子在其天然启动子和完整 基因组 存在的情况下在分化的上皮细胞中组装。在这里,我们利用这个系统来证明,在更自然的环境中产生的野生型 HPV18,可以从上游甲硫氨酸(共有甲硫氨酸上游的 61 个氨基酸残基)翻译出较大形式的 L1,以及从共有甲硫氨酸中翻译出较小的形式,两种尺寸都在新形成的病毒体中组装。61位上游甲硫氨酸残基的消融改变了病毒粒子衣壳构象,并且还降低了病毒粒子稳定性和感染性。重要性 本研究调查乳头瘤病毒病毒颗粒是否含有不止一种 L1 主要衣壳蛋白亚型。通过使用模仿自然分化上皮的器官型筏培养物,我们发现野生型 HPV18 表达两种不同的 L1 亚型并将其整合到病毒粒子中,包括从上游甲硫氨酸翻译而来的以前未被识别的较长形式。我们的研究进一步表明,上游蛋氨酸的破坏会损害病毒粒子的稳定性和感染性,证明较长的 L1 亚型有助于适当的衣壳结构和病毒功能。这些发现提供了对 HPV 衣壳生物学的新认识,并对 HPV 疫苗、诊断和 抗病毒药物 疗法的未来发展具有重要意义。

title: A fluorescence-based reporter system to monitor human papillomavirus E2-dependent reporter activation in keratinocytes
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) gene regulation is closely linked to epithelial biology, but simple experimental systems for visualizing functional viral transcriptional activity in keratinocytes remain limited. This study presents a fluorescence-based reporter system designed to monitor HPV E2-dependent reporter activation in HaCaT keratinocytes. Using an enhanced green fluorescent protein (GFP) reporter controlled by an E2-responsive promoter cassette, the system enables direct microscopic visualization and semiquantitative image-based analysis of reporter activation. Cotransfection with an HPV16 early-region plasmid increased normalized GFP signal compared with reporter-only controls, supporting the use of this platform as a reproducible proof-of-principle assay. The system is not intended as a diagnostic test or infectivity assay, but provides a technically simple experimental tool for studying HPV-related transcriptional regulation in vitro.

title: Contemporary High-risk Human Papillomavirus Genotype Distribution and Associated Cytologic Findings Using Extended Human Papillomavirus Genotyping
abstract: Objectives: In January 2024, our laboratory implemented a human papillomavirus (HPV) assay that detects 14 high-risk HPV (hrHPV) genotypes—6 individually and 8 in 3 pooled groups. We evaluated genotype-specific infections and cytologic outcomes over 1 year to assess trends in HPV-related pathology. Methods: After institutional review board exemption, a retrospective review of hrHPV tests and corresponding Papanicolaou cytology diagnoses of positive hrHPV tests from January to December 2024 was performed. Results: Of 43,017 HPV tests, 3,771 (8.8%) were hrHPV-positive. Among 3,015 hrHPV-positive cases with corresponding cytologic diagnoses, 2,374 (78.7%) and 641 (21.3%) exhibited single hrHPV detections and multiple-genotype infections, respectively. Within the multiple-genotype group, HPV16 was detected in 129 cases—19 with HSIL—and HPV18 was present in 68 cases—8 with HSIL. Pooled genotypes 56/59/66 and 35/39/68 were each detected in 328 cases—6 total with HSIL. Single-genotype infections exhibited similar trends. Although multiple-genotype infections showed a higher frequency of high-grade lesions, these cases were predominantly associated with the presence of HPV16 and/or HPV18. Conclusions: Extended genotyping demonstrated that pooled non-16/18 genotype groups comprised nearly half of hrHPV-positive infections and were predominantly associated with negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance, and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions on cytology. Although HPV16 and 18 remained the genotypes most strongly associated with high-grade cytologic abnormalities, the high prevalence of non-16/18 genotypes highlights the importance of genotype surveillance in the postvaccination era. These findings support the value of extended genotyping for risk stratification and population-level monitoring of evolving HPV epidemiology.
journal: Journal of Lower Genital Tract Disease

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes and their association with cytologic findings using extended genotyping. The research aimed to address the need for updated surveillance in the postvaccination era by analyzing 43,017 HPV tests conducted between January and December 2024. The results showed that 8.8% of tests were hrHPV-positive, with 78.7% of cases involving single-genotype infections and 21.3% involving multiple-genotype infections. The study found that HPV16 and HPV18 were most frequently associated with high-grade lesions, while pooled non-16/18 groups were linked to lower-grade abnormalities. These findings highlight the value of extended genotyping for risk stratification and monitoring HPV epidemiology. The study's limitations include its retrospective design and single-year timeframe, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

abstract_zh: 目标:2024 年 1 月,我们的实验室实施了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 检测,可检测 14 种 高危型HPV (hrHPV) 基因型——6 种单独检测,8 种分为 3 个混合组。我们评估了一年多的基因型特异性感染和细胞学结果,以评估 HPV 相关病理学的趋势。方法:在机构审查委员会豁免后,对 2024 年 1 月至 12 月的 hrHPV 检测和相应的 hrHPV 检测阳性的巴氏细胞学诊断进行回顾性审查。结果:在 43,017 项 HPV 检测中,3,771 项 (8.8%) 为 hrHPV 阳性。在 3,015 例具有相应细胞学诊断的 hrHPV 阳性病例中,分别有 2,374 例(78.7%)和 641 例(21.3%)表现出单一 hrHPV 检测和多基因型感染。在多基因型组中,129 例病例中检测到 HPV16(其中 19 例患有 HSIL),68 例病例中检测到 HPV18(8 例患有 HSIL)。在 328 例病例中分别检测到了混合基因型 56/59/66 和 35/39/68,总共 6 例患有 HSIL。单基因型感染也表现出类似的趋势。尽管多基因型感染显示高级别病变的频率较高,但这些病例主要与 HPV16 和/或 HPV18 的存在相关。结论:扩展基因分型表明,合并的非 16/18 基因型组包括近一半的 hrHPV 阳性感染,并且主要与上皮内病变或恶性肿瘤阴性、意义未明的非典型鳞状细胞以及细胞学上的低度鳞状上皮内病变相关。尽管 HPV16 和 18 仍然是与高度细胞学异常最密切相关的基因型,但非 16/18 基因型的高 监测 凸显了基因型 监测 在疫苗接种后时代的重要性。这些研究结果支持了扩展基因分型对于不断演变的 HPV 流行病学 的风险分层和人群水平监测的价值。

title: Risk factors for persistent high-risk HPV infection and recurrence burden of vaginal infections in women with cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection drives cervical carcinogenesis, yet factors determining persistence in women with low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) remain incompletely characterized. The longitudinal recurrence burden of vaginal infections including aerobic vaginitis, bacterial vaginosis, and vulvovaginal candidiasis in this population has not been systematically quantified. Objective To identify independent risk factors for persistent HR-HPV infection and evaluate the recurrence burden of aerobic vaginitis, bacterial vaginosis, and vulvovaginal candidiasis in women with cervical LSIL. Study design This retrospective cohort study included 3,563 women with cervical LSIL who underwent concurrent vaginal microecology testing, HPV genotyping, and cervical cytology at Guangdong Women and Children Hospital (January 2021–August 2025). Patients were classified as persistent (n=919; ≥365 days with the same HR-HPV subtype) or transient (n=2,644; >30 days and <365 days). Multivariate logistic regression identified factors associated with persistence. Negative binomial regression assessed recurrence burden, expressed as incidence density per 100 person-years. Results After adjustment, age (per 5 years: OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.09–1.17, P<0.001), HPV-52/58 (OR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.38–1.98, P<0.001), and multiple HR-HPV infections (OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.24–1.81, P<0.001) independently predicted persistence. Bacterial vaginosis (OR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.55–0.88, P = 0.002) and intermediate bacterial vaginosis (OR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.52–0.84, P<0.001), and vulvovaginal candidiasis (OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.58–0.96, P = 0.024) showed inverse associations. Among persistently infected women, aerobic vaginitis had the highest recurrence burden (35.77 per 100 person-years, 95% CI: 33.17–38.53), exceeding bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis. Persistent infection was associated with TCT abnormalities ≥ASC-US (OR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.40–1.91, P<0.001) and LSIL+ lesions (OR = 1.48, 95% CI: 1.25–1.75, P<0.001). Conclusion HPV-52/58, multiple HR-HPV infections, and advancing age significantly increase persistence risk in LSIL patients. The inverse associations of bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis with persistence are likely non-causal and should be interpreted with caution. The high aerobic vaginitis recurrence burden underscores the need for integrated management addressing both viral persistence and vaginal dysbiosis. These findings support genotype- and microbiota-informed risk stratification.

title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Infection-Associated Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition: Implication in Tumorigenesis and Pathogenesis of HPV-Positive Cancers
abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastases. This structured narrative review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung, and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT may contribute to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links may exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors may influence their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. The relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is delineated as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators, etc. The review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review explores the role of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in HPV infection and its implications for tumorigenesis and pathogenesis of HPV-positive cancers. It specifically addresses how HPV-driven EMT contributes to malignant transformation, the mechanistic links between HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and the influence of EMT on treatment outcomes and pathogenesis of various HPV-positive tumors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a structured narrative synthesis focusing on the molecular interactions between HPV and EMT. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis procedures. The review method is based on a comprehensive analysis of the literature related to HPV and EMT, with an emphasis on molecular crosstalk and its role in cancer progression.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV infection is associated with EMT in human epithelial cells, which contributes to the development of HPV-positive cancers. It highlights the complex multicomponent mechanism involving ligand-receptor interactions, transcription factors, signaling pathways, and epigenetic regulators that link HPV infection to EMT. The findings suggest that EMT plays a critical role in the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in understanding the precise mechanisms by which HPV triggers EMT and its role in different HPV-positive cancers. It also notes that while EMT is implicated in tumor invasion and metastasis, the exact contribution of EMT to treatment outcomes and resistance remains unclear. These gaps highlight the need for further research into the molecular pathways and their clinical relevance.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets could be valuable for the prevention, prediction, and treatment of HPV-induced cancers. It emphasizes the importance of investigating these biomarkers in clinical settings to improve early detection and therapeutic strategies for HPV-positive malignancies.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the role of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers. It highlights the molecular mechanisms linking HPV infection to EMT, including ligand-receptor interactions, transcription factors, and signaling pathways. The study emphasizes that EMT contributes to tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant transformation in HPV-positive cancers. While the review identifies potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers in cancer prevention and treatment, it also notes unresolved questions about the precise mechanisms and clinical implications of EMT in HPV-induced malignancies. The findings underscore the need for further research to clarify the role of EMT in different HPV-positive tumor types and to develop targeted interventions.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一个结构化的叙述性综合,重点关注 HPV 和 EMT 之间的分子相互作用。它不报告特定的数据库、检索日期或荟萃分析程序。该综述方法基于对HPV和EMT相关文献的综合分析,重点关注分子串扰及其在癌症进展中的作用。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,HPV 感染与人类上皮细胞的 EMT 相关,这有助于 HPV 阳性癌症的发展。它强调了复杂的多组分机制,涉及配体-受体相互作用、转录因子、信号通路和将 HPV 感染与 EMT 联系起来的表观遗传调节因子。研究结果表明EMT在HPV感染的上皮细胞的恶性转化中发挥着关键作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出了在了解 HPV 触发 EMT 的精确机制及其在不同 HPV 阳性癌症中的作用方面存在的差距。它还指出,虽然 EMT 与肿瘤侵袭和转移有关,但 EMT 对 治疗 结果和耐药性的确切贡献仍不清楚。这些差距突出表明需要进一步研究分子途径及其临床相关性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,EMT 相关生物标志物和分子靶点对于 HPV 诱发的癌症的预防、预测和 治疗 可能有价值。它强调了在临床环境中研究这些生物标志物以改善 HPV 阳性恶性肿瘤的早期检测和治疗策略的重要性。

abstract_zh: 上皮间质转化(EMT)是一个程序化的可逆过程,允许上皮细胞暂时获得具有增强的迁移和侵袭能力的间充质细胞表型。类似的表型调节也可以发生在癌细胞中,癌细胞在经历 EMT 后,表现出癌症干细胞样特性并主动迁移,导致肿瘤侵袭和转移。这篇结构化叙述性综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和 EMT 之间的分子串扰,这种串扰发生在 HPV 感染的人类上皮和不同部位(宫颈、头颈、结直肠、肺癌等)的 HPV 阳性癌症中。这里讨论的主要问题是:(i)HPV驱动的EMT如何促进HPV感染的上皮细胞的恶性转化,(ii)人类癌症中HPV阳性和EMT之间可能存在什么机制联系,以及(iii)各种HPV阳性人类肿瘤中的EMT如何影响其发病机制、治疗模式和结果。HPV感染与EMT程序之间的关系被描述为由外源性和内源性刺激触发的复杂的多组分机制,涉及特定的配体-受体相互作用、膜通道、转录因子、信号通路、表观遗传调节因子等。该综述还讨论了EMT相关生物标志物和分子靶点在HPV诱导的癌症的预防、预测和治疗中的一些潜在应用。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一个结构化的叙述性综合,重点关注 HPV 和 EMT 之间的分子相互作用。它不报告特定的数据库、检索日期或荟萃分析程序。该综述方法基于对HPV和EMT相关文献的综合分析,重点关注分子串扰及其在癌症进展中的作用。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,HPV 感染与人类上皮细胞的 EMT 相关,这有助于 HPV 阳性癌症的发展。它强调了复杂的多组分机制,涉及配体-受体相互作用、转录因子、信号通路和将 HPV 感染与 EMT 联系起来的表观遗传调节因子。研究结果表明EMT在HPV感染的上皮细胞的恶性转化中发挥着关键作用。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出了在了解 HPV 触发 EMT 的精确机制及其在不同 HPV 阳性癌症中的作用方面存在的差距。它还指出,虽然 EMT 与肿瘤侵袭和转移有关,但 EMT 对 治疗 结果和耐药性的确切贡献仍不清楚。这些差距突出表明需要进一步研究分子途径及其临床相关性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,EMT 相关生物标志物和分子靶点对于 HPV 诱发的癌症的预防、预测和 治疗 可能有价值。它强调了在临床环境中研究这些生物标志物以改善 HPV 阳性恶性肿瘤的早期检测和治疗策略的重要性。

title: Development and Laboratory Evaluation of a Standardized Procedure for Environmental Sampling and Molecular Detection of Human Papillomavirus
abstract: Abstract Background Environmental surveillance of infectious pathogens is increasingly important for disease prevention and control; however, heterogeneity in sampling, preservation, and transport procedures can substantially affect molecular detection results. Methods Human papillomavirus (HPV) was used as a non-enveloped DNA virus model to evaluate six determinants of surface sampling performance: swab type, surface material, sampling interval, swab pre-moistening, ambient temperature, and preservation medium. An HPV-positive inoculum was prepared by pooling approximately 150 anonymized male urethral swab specimens, followed by saline elution, genotype confirmation, and quantitative testing. HPV DNA was quantified by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR). Outcomes were the positive detection rate and a prespecified log-scale recovery index. Results Polyester and sponge swabs achieved the highest positive detection rates (both 98.04% ± 3.40%), whereas polyester swabs had the highest mean log-scale recovery index. HPV DNA was more readily recovered from smooth, non-porous, non-absorbent surfaces (ceramic tile and polypropylene) than from wood or woven fabric. Dry polyester swabbing yielded a higher positive detection rate than PBS-pre-moistened swabbing (88.75% ± 2.80% vs 80.00% ± 5.23%; P = 0.032), although the log-scale recovery index did not differ significantly. Sampling from 1 to 24 h after inoculation did not significantly affect either outcome. Exposure to 35°C reduced both the positive detection rate and the log-scale recovery index compared with 15°C and 25°C. Dedicated viral transport media maintained HPV DNA detectability throughout 28 days of storage at 2–8°C. PBS first fell below the prespecified 70% detection threshold on day 7, whereas normal saline remained at or above the threshold through 3 h and fell below it at 6 h. Conclusions Under the tested laboratory conditions, dry polyester swabs combined with dedicated viral transport media provided the most practical overall approach for molecular recovery of HPV from environmental surfaces. Surface properties and ambient temperature were the principal determinants of HPV DNA detectability. These findings support protocol standardization but do not establish viral infectivity or fomite transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different sampling and preservation methods for detecting human papillomavirus (HPV) in environmental settings. Using HPV as a model, the researchers tested factors such as swab type, surface material, temperature, and preservation medium. They found that polyester and sponge swabs had the highest positive detection rates, while smooth surfaces like ceramic tile and polypropylene yielded better DNA recovery. The study also showed that higher temperatures reduced detection rates, and dedicated viral transport media maintained HPV DNA detectability for up to 28 days. The results suggest that standardizing protocols with dry polyester swabs and appropriate transport media could improve molecular recovery of HPV from environmental surfaces. However, the study does not address viral infectivity or transmission through fomites. The evidence is limited to laboratory conditions and does not provide information on real-world applicability or potential confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 传染性病原体的环境监测对于疾病预防和控制越来越重要;然而,采样、保存和运输程序的异质性会严重影响分子检测结果。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)作为无包膜DNA病毒模型来评估表面采样性能的六个决定因素:拭子类型、表面材料、采样间隔、拭子预湿、环境温度和保存介质。
elements_zh.methods: 通过汇集大约 150 个匿名男性尿道拭子样本,然后进行盐水洗脱、基因型确认和定量检测,制备 HPV 阳性接种物。通过实时定量 PCR (qPCR) 对 HPV DNA 进行定量。
elements_zh.main_results: 聚酯拭子和海绵拭子的阳性检出率最高(均为 98.04% ± 3.40%),而聚酯拭子的平均对数标度回收指数最高。与木材或机织织物相比,从光滑、无孔、非吸收性表面(瓷砖和聚丙烯)更容易回收 HPV DNA。与 15°C 和 25°C 相比,暴露在 35°C 下会降低阳性检出率和对数标度回收指数。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在经过测试的实验室条件下,干燥聚酯拭子与专用病毒运输介质相结合,为从环境表面回收 HPV 分子提供了最实用的整体方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持方案标准化,但并未确定病毒传染性或污染物 传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究结果对现实世界环境的普遍性或混杂因素的存在。

title: Understanding the implementation and scale up of human papillomavirus testing using self-sampling techniques and point-of-care diagnostics for the screening of cervical cancer in Malawi
abstract: Background: Although cervical cancer is one of the most preventable malignancies worldwide, Malawi remains among the top five countries globally with the highest incidence and mortality rates from cervical cancer. The country’s screening programme is largely based on a screen-and-treat strategy using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. Despite nationwide roll-out, screening coverage remains low and inequitable. The World Health Organization (WHO) now recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) DNA testing – which demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy as opposed to VIA – as the preferred screening method. Emerging point-of-care (POC) HPV tests and self-sampling modalities have shown potential to transform screening accessibility in low-resource settings such as Malawi. This thesis explores the feasibility of integrating POC HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening programme. Objectives: This work had five main aims: (1) to describe the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi; (2) to quantify and describe the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilisation; (3) to evaluate the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework; (4) to explore the acceptability of cervical self-sampling among women; and (5) to assess the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting. Findings: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favouring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible. Implications: These findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. Integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings. The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the feasibility of integrating point-of-care HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into Malawi's cervical cancer screening program. It highlights the limitations of the current VIA-based approach and the potential of HPV testing to improve coverage and equity. The research demonstrates that self-sampling is highly acceptable and that POC HPV testing is operationally feasible in rural areas. These findings support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing and have informed national guidelines. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit its depth. The evidence suggests a moderate confidence in the feasibility of these interventions in low-resource settings.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a significant public health issue in Malawi, with high incidence and mortality rates despite existing screening programs. The study aimed to explore the feasibility of integrating point-of-care HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening program.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the Malawian cervical cancer screening program, which primarily uses visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. It examined the impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilization and assessed the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing in rural southern Malawi.
analysis_en.methods: The study described the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi, quantified the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on health service utilization, and evaluated the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework. It also explored the acceptability of self-sampling among women and assessed the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting.
analysis_en.main_results: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favoring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high, and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. The study demonstrates that integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on an abstract-only analysis, which may limit the depth of understanding. However, the evidence is sufficient to support the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting, with a moderate confidence level.

title_zh: 了解使用自采样技术和护理点诊断在马拉维筛查 人乳头瘤病毒 的 人乳头瘤病毒 测试的实施和扩大
source_body_en: Background: Although cervical cancer is one of the most preventable malignancies worldwide, Malawi remains among the top five countries globally with the highest incidence and mortality rates from cervical cancer. The country’s screening programme is largely based on a screen-and-treat strategy using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. Despite nationwide roll-out, screening coverage remains low and inequitable. The World Health Organization (WHO) now recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) DNA testing – which demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy as opposed to VIA – as the preferred screening method. Emerging point-of-care (POC) HPV tests and self-sampling modalities have shown potential to transform screening accessibility in low-resource settings such as Malawi. This thesis explores the feasibility of integrating POC HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening programme. Objectives: This work had five main aims: (1) to describe the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi; (2) to quantify and describe the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilisation; (3) to evaluate the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework; (4) to explore the acceptability of cervical self-sampling among women; and (5) to assess the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting. Findings: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favouring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible. Implications: These findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. Integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings. The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.

title: INFLUÊNCIA DA MICROBIOTA VAGINAL NA PERSISTÊNCIA DA INFECÇÃO PELO HPV E NA PROGRESSÃO DAS LESÕES CERVICAIS: UMA REVISÃO DA LITERATURA INFLUENCE OF VAGINAL MICROBIOTA ON HPV INFECTION PERSISTENCE AND CERVICAL LESION PROGRESSION: A LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: A infecção pelo papilomavírus humano (HPV), especialmente pelos tipos de alto risco, está relacionada ao desenvolvimento de lesões intraepiteliais cervicais e ao câncer de colo do útero. Embora a persistência viral seja um dos principais fatores envolvidos nesse processo, evidências recentes indicam que a composição da microbiota vaginal pode estar relacionada à evolução da infecção. Esse artigo buscou analisar a influência da microbiota vaginal na persistência da infecção pelo HPV e na progressão das lesões cervicais. Foi realizada uma revisão da literatura nas bases PubMed e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), utilizando os descritores “Microbiota”, “Papillomavirus Infections” e “Uterine Cervical Dysplasia”, combinados pelo operador booleano AND. Foram selecionados 25 estudos publicados nos últimos cinco anos, disponíveis gratuitamente e em texto completo. Os resultados demonstraram associação entre disbiose cervicovaginal, alterações na composição de espécies de Lactobacillus e persistência do HPV, além de relações com diferentes graus de lesão cervical. Também foram observadas alterações em bactérias anaeróbias e em perfis metabólicos relacionados à resposta imune local. Conclui-se que a microbiota vaginal pode participar do microambiente associado à persistência do HPV e à progressão das lesões, embora a relação causal ainda não esteja completamente estabelecida.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the influence of vaginal microbiota on HPV infection persistence and cervical lesion progression. It highlights the association between vaginal dysbiosis, changes in Lactobacillus species composition, and HPV persistence, as well as links to varying degrees of cervical lesions. Alterations in anaerobic bacteria and metabolic profiles related to local immune response were also observed. While the role of vaginal microbiota in shaping the microenvironment for HPV persistence and lesion progression is suggested, a causal relationship remains unestablished.
